Du bist der offizielle KI-Kurations-Assistent für das autodocs Dokumentations- und Spezifikationssystem (AUTOSAR & S-Core).
Deine Aufgabe ist es, präzise, fachlich fundierte Erklärungen, User Guides und Diagramme zu verfassen.

FOLGENDE RICHTLINIEN SIND STRIKT BINDEND:
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nThis document contains the requirements on the functionality, API and the configura-\ntion of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Communication Management as part of the Adaptive\nAUTOSAR platform foundation.\nThe Communication Management realizes Service Oriented Communication between\nAdaptive AUTOSAR Applications for all levels of communication, e.g. IntraProcess, In-\nterProcess, InterMachine. It consists of potentially generated Service Provider Skele-\ntons and Service Requester Proxies and optionally the generic Communication Man-\nager software for central brokering and configuration.\nThe Communication Management provides a built-in safety mechanism (E2E protec-\ntion), which can be used for all levels of communication for events and methods.\nThe documentation of the Communication Management consists of two documents:\n\u000f\nthe ARAComAPI explanatory document [1], providing explanations of the design\nand behavior descriptions of the ara::com API,\n\u000f\nthis document, providing the requirements on the ara::com API.\nTherefore it is recommended to read the ARAComAPI explanatory document first to\nget an overview and understanding, and to read this document afterward.\n13 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Limitations\nThe current version of this document is missing some functionality which is not stan-\ndardized and specified within the\nSWS Communication Management\ndocument but\ndescribed in\nExplanation of ara::com API\n[1] and implemented in the demonstrator\ncode:\n4.1.1 Local Buffer Overruns\nCurrently it is not specified what happens if local buffers are full because the application\naccesses data slower than they are received over the network.\n4.1.2 SOME/IP\nThe following limitations regarding the SOME/IP functionality described in [4] and [5]\napply:\n4.1.2.1 Optional method arguments with Tag-Length-Value serialization\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00001]\n{DRAFT}\nOptional method arguments with SOME/IP\nTag-Length-Value serialization\nd\nCommunication Management does currently not\nsupport the existence of optional method arguments with the Tag-Length-Value seri-\nalization principle (described in [4] and [5].\nc\n()\n)\n4.1.3 SOME/IP Service Discovery\nThe following limitations regarding the SOME/IP SD functionality described in [6] and\n[5] apply:\n4.1.3.1 SOME/IP Service Discovery Discardable flag\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00002]\n{DRAFT}\nSOME/IP Service Discovery Discardable\nflag\nd\nThe specification does not support setting the SOME/IP Service Discovery Dis-\ncardable flag of a SOME/IP entry option to 1 and reacting to the reception of an (un-\nknown/unsupported) option with the Discardable flag set to 1 (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_-\n00273], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00275], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00276], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_-\n00544]).\nc\n()\n19 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4.1.3.2 SOME/IP Service Discovery Configuration options\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00003]\n{DRAFT}\nSOME/IP Service Discovery Configuration\noptions\nd\nThe specification does not support that SOME/IP Service Discovery con-\nfiguration options (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00276] - [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00287]) con-\nfigured via the\nRequiredSomeipServiceInstance\n.\ncapabilityRecord\nrespec-\ntively in the\nProvidedSomeipServiceInstance\n.\ncapabilityRecord\nand config-\nuration options contained in a FindService respectively OfferService entry of a received\nSOME/IP-SD message are considered during the process of matching offered services\nto required services and vice versa. Any configured and/or received configuration op-\ntions are simply ignored during the matching process, i.e., they don't have any impact\non the result set returned by FindService() or StartFindService().       "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_10445] [SWS_CM_10454]\n[SWS_CM_10455] [SWS_CM_10456]\n[SWS_CM_10457] [SWS_CM_99036]\n[SWS_CM_99037] [SWS_CM_99038]\n[SWS_CM_99039]"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P54_206",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 54,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7 Functional specification\n7.1 General description\nThe AUTOSAR Adaptive architecture organizes the software of the AUTOSAR Adap-\ntive foundation as functional clusters. These clusters offer common functionality as\nservices to the applications. The Communication Management (CM) for AUTOSAR\nAdaptive is such a functional cluster and is part of \"AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive\nApplications\" - ARA. It is responsible for the construction and supervision of communi-\ncation paths between applications, both local and remote.\nThe CM provides the infrastructure that enables communication between Adaptive\nAUTOSAR Applications within one machine and with software entities on other ma-\nchines, e.g. other Adaptive AUTOSAR applications or Classic AUTOSAR SWCs. All\ncommunication paths can be established at design- , start-up- or run-time.\nThis specification includes the syntax of the API, the relationship of API to the model\nand describes semantics, e.g. through state machines, and assumption of pre-, post-\nconditions and use of APIs. The specification does not provide constraints on the SW\narchitecture of a platform implementation, so there is no definition of basic software\nmodules and no specification of implementation or internal technical architecture of\nthe Communication Management.\n7.1.1 Architectural concepts\nThe Communication management of AUTOSAR Adaptive can be logically divided into\nthe following sub-parts:\n\u000f\nLanguage binding\n\u000f\nEnd-to-end communication protection\n\u000f\nCommunication / Network binding\n\u000f\nCommunication Management software\n54 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P55_207",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 55,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P55_208",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 55,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.1: Technical Architecture of Communication Management\nIn the context of Communication Management, the following types of interfaces are\ndefined:\n\u000f\nPublic Application Interface: Part of the Adaptive AUTOSAR API and specified in\nthe SWS. This is the standardized ara::com API.\n\u000f\nFunctional Cluster Interactions: Interaction between functional clusters. Not nor-\nmative, intended to make specification more readable and to support integration\nof SW into demonstrator. (dotted arrow in 7.1) And also interactions between\nelements within a functional cluster. Not used in specifications, so it is a non-\nstandardized interface. Used for communication inside Communication Manage-\nment software (grey arrow in 7.1)\nPlease note, that Language Binding and Communication Binding depend on a specific\nconfiguration by the integrator, but they need to be deployed within the application\nbinary. This results in the fact that the serialization of the Communication Binding will\nrun in the execution context of the Adaptive Application.\nFor the design of ARA API the following constraints apply:\n\u000f\nSupport the independence of application software components\n\u000f\nUse of Service-oriented communication without dependency on a specific com-\nmunication protocol\n55 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P56_209",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 56,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nMake the API as lean as possible, neither supporting very specific use cases\nwhich could also be done on top of the API, nor supporting component model\nor higher level concepts. The API is restricted to support core communication\nmechanisms.\n\u000f\nSupport for dynamic communication:\n\nNo discovery by application middleware, the clients know the server but the\nServer does not know the clients. Event subscription is the only dynamic\ncommunication pattern in the application.\n\nFull service discovery in the application. No communication paths are known\nat configuration time. An API for Service discovery allows the application\ncode to choose the service instance.\n\u000f\nSupport both Event/Callback and Polling style usage of the API to enable classic\nRTE style paradigms. To support high determinism demands in case of callback-\nbased / event-based interaction, there shall be the possibility to avoid uncontrolled\ncontext switches.\n\u000f\nSupport both synchronous callback-based communication and asynchronous\ncommunication philosophy.\n\u000f\nSupport of client/server communication.\n\u000f\nSupport of sender/receiver communication with queued semantics where the re-\nceiver caches are configurable.\n\u000f\nSupport of selection of trigger conditions for task activation.\n\u000f\nExtensions for security.\n\u000f\nExtensions for Quality Of Service QoS.\n\u000f\nScalability for real-time systems.\n\u000f\nSupport of built-in end-to-end communication protection, where a use-case-\nspecific behavior can be done on top of ARA API.\n7.1.2 Design decisions\nThe design of the ARA API covers the following principles:\n\u000f\nIt uses the Proxy/Skeleton pattern:\n\nThe (service) proxy is the representative of the possibly remote (i.e. other\nprocess, other core, other node) service. It is an instance of a C++ class\nlocal to the application/client, which uses the service.\n\nThe (service) skeleton is the connection of the user provided service imple-\nmentation to the middleware transport infrastructure. Service implementa-\ntion class is derived from the (service) skeleton.\n56 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P57_210",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 57,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\nBeside proxies/skeletons, there might exist a so-called \"Runtime\" (singleton)\nclass to provide some essentials to manage proxies and skeletons. But\nthis is communication management software implementation specific and\ntherefore not specified in this document, but may be specified in a future\nversion.\nRegarding proxy/skeleton design pattern in general and its role in middleware\nimplementations, see [11] [12].\n\u000f\nIt supports callback mechanisms on data reception.\n\u000f\nThe API has zero-copy capabilities including the possibility for memory manage-\nment in the middleware.\n\u000f\nIt is aligned with the AUTOSAR service model (services, instances, events, meth-\nods, ...) to allow the generation of proxies and skeletons out of this model.\n\u000f\nFull discovery and service instance selection support on API level.\n\u000f\nClient/Server Communication uses concepts introduced by C++11 language, e.g.\nstd::future, std::promise, to fully support method calls between different contexts.\n\u000f\nAbstract from SOME/IP specific behavior, but support SOME/IP service mecha-\nnisms, as methods, events and fields.\n\u000f\nSupport/implement the standard end-to-end protection protocols, as specified in\n[9] and [7].\n\u000f\nSupport of Service contract versioning.\n\u000f\nSupport Event and Polling style usage of the API equally to enable classic RT\nstyle paradigms.\n\u000f\nFully exploit C++11/14 features in API design to provide usability and comfort for\nthe application developer.\nSee ARAComAPI explanatory [1] for more details and explanations on the ARA API\ndesign.\n7.1.3 Communication paradigms and Definitions\nService-Oriented Communication (SoC) as a part of Service-Oriented Architecture\n(SOA) [13] is the main communication pattern for Adaptive AUTOSAR Applications.\nIt allows establishing communication paths both at run-time, so it can be used to build\nup dynamic communication with unknown number of participants. Figure 7.2 shows\nthe basic operation principle of Service-Oriented Communication.\n57 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P58_211",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_12002",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 58,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P58_212",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_12002",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 58,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.2: Service-Oriented Communication\nService Discovery decides whether external and internal service-oriented communi-\ncation is established. The discovery strategy shall allow either returning a specific\nservice instance or all available instances providing the requested service at the time\nof the request, no matter if they are available locally or remote. The Communication\nManagement software should provide an optimized implementation for both the Ser-\nvice discovery and the communication connection, depending on the location where\nthe service provider resides. More about Service Discovery can be found in\nSOME/IP\nService Discovery Protocol Specification\n[6].\nThe service class is the central element of the Service-Oriented Communication pat-\ntern applied in Adaptive AUTOSAR. It represents the service by collecting the methods\nand events which are provided or requested by the applications implementing the con-\ncrete service functionality.\n[SWS_CM_12002]\n{DRAFT}\nActive subscriber\nd\nThe active subscriber shall be an\nadaptive application that has invoked the Subscribe method of the respective:\n\u000f\nTrigger class (see [SWS_CM_00723]) or\n\u000f\nField or Event class (see [SWS_CM_00141])\nand has not canceled the subscription by invoking the Unsubscribe method of the re-\nspective:\n\u000f\nTrigger class (see [SWS_CM_00810]) or\n\u000f\nField or Event class (see [SWS_CM_00151])\nc\n(RS_CM_00103, RS_AP_00114, RS_AP_00120)\n[SWS_CM_12003]\n{DRAFT}\nActive subscriber when SOME/IP Network binding is\nused\nd\nIn addition to [SWS_CM_12002], if SOME/IP Network binding is used to provide\n58 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P59_213",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00205",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 59,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nservices for an application, the active subscriber shall be an adaptive application for\nwhich the SOME/IP services subscription has not yet expired when the TTL contained\nin the respective SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message has been exceeded (see\n[SWS_CM_00205]).\nc\n(RS_CM_00103, RS_AP_00114, RS_AP_00120)\n7.1.4 Service contract versioning\nIn Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) environments the client and the provider of\na service rely on a contract which covers the service interface and behavior. The\ninterface and the behavior of a service may change over time. Therefore, service\ncontract versioning has been introduced to differentiate between the different versions\nof a service."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P60_214",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99003",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 60,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P60_215",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99003",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 60,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.4: Service contract versioning flow\nNote:\n1. The contract version of a\nServiceInterface\nconsists of a\nmajorVersion\nand a\nminorVersion\nnumber. The\nmajorVersion\nnumber indicates backwards-\nincompatible service changes. The\nminorVersion\nnumber indicates backwards-\ncompatible service changes.\n\u000f\nfor backwards-incompatible interface or behavior changes the\nmajorVersion\nnumber is increased and the\nminorVersion\nnumber is set to 0.\n\u000f\nfor backwards-compatible interface or behavior changes the\nmajorVersion\nnumber is unchanged and the\nminorVersion\nnumber is increased.\n2. The contract version of a\nServiceInterface\nis mapped to a version of the\nServiceInterfaceDeployment\n. This version mapping may be done several times\nresulting in several\nServiceInterfaceDeployment\ns for the same\nServiceIn-\nterface\n.       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2 Communication Group\nNOTE:\nCommunication Groups have been set to obsolete and will be removed or re-\nplaced in the next AUTOSAR release(s).\nThe Communication Group is a communication concept based on\nara::com\nwhich is\ndesigned for Adaptive State Management applications. It can be seen as a composite\nService which manages information routing in a defined manner. A Communication\nGroup has one server and multiple clients. The server is able to send broadcast and\npeer to peer messages to the clients of a Communication Group. The clients can\nacknowledge these messages. The server of a Communication Group can further\nverify how many clients are connected to the Communication Group at every time.\nApplications can connect/disconnect to a Communication Group instance using one of\nthe two Communication Group Service Interfaces,\nCommunicationGroupServer\nor\nCommunicationGroupClient\n."

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.2 Behavior\nThe Communication Group performs the following tasks to enable a Communication\nGroup.\n[SWS_CM_99010]\n{OBSOLETE}\nBroadcast task\nd\nA Broadcast task shall be triggered\nby the\nbroadcast\nmethod of the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService. The Com-\nmunicationGroup shall forward this broadcast message to all connected clients by call-\ning the\nmessage\nmethod of the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService from each\nconnected client.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99011]\n{OBSOLETE}\nPeer To Peer message task\nd\nA Peer to Peer mes-\nsage task shall be triggered by the\nmessage\nmethod (which includes the client ad-\ndress) of the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService. The CommunicationGroup\nshall forward this message to the addressed client by calling the\nmessage\nmethod\nof the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService of this client.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_-\nCM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99012]\n{OBSOLETE}\nMessage Response task\nd\nThe Message Response\ntask shall be triggered by the\nmessage response\nevent of the\nCommunication-\nGroupClient\nService from a client . The CommunicationGroup shall forward this\nresponse message with the client source address to the\nmessage response\nevent\nof the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99013]\n{OBSOLETE}\nList Clients task\nd\nThe List Clients task shall be trig-\ngered by the\nlist clients\nmethod of the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService.\nThe CommunicationGroup shall provide the list of all connected client addresses with\nthe return of the\nlist clients\nmethod of the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nSer-\nvice.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n7.2.3 Connection\nThe connection and disconnection to Communication Group is performed by standard\nara::com\nfunctions.\n7.2.3.1 Communication Group Server\nThe Server of a Communication Group connects to a Communication Group by con-\nnecting to the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService of this Communication group\n(using\nFindService\nor\nStartFindService\n).\n[SWS_CM_99016]\n{OBSOLETE}\nConnection Status of a Communication Group\nServer\nd\nThe Server of the Communication Group shall be considered to be connected\nif the server has successfully subscribed to the response\nmessage response\nevent\nof the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService, else the Server shall be considered\nnot connected.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n64 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.3.2 Communication Group Client\nA Communication Group client connects to a Communication Group by offering the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService. A Communication Group client disconnects\nto a Communication Group by stop offering the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nSer-\nvice.\n7.2.4 Limitations\nThe Communication Group concept has the following limitations:\n\u000f\nThere is only one Server for an instance of a Communication Group at a given\ntime.\n\u000f\nA Client provides the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService to only one in-\nstance of a Communication Group at a given time.\nThe figure below outlines a connection example for a Communication Group."

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nThe event definition according to [SWS_CM_99009] shall define the data type of\nthe\nmessage responses\nof the Communication Group.\n\u000f\nThe method definition according to [SWS_CM_99008] shall define the data type\nof the\nmessages\nof the Communication Group.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\nBased on the Communication Group\ntemplate\n[SWS_CM_99020] the\nServiceIn-\nterface\ns for the\nCommunicationGroupServer\n[SWS_CM_99000] and the\nCom-\nmunicationGroupClient\n[SWS_CM_99007] can be generated/derived.\n[SWS_CM_99021]\n{OBSOLETE}\nSHORT-NAME\nvalue of generated\nCommunica-\ntionGroupServer\nservice\nd\nThe\nSHORT-NAME\nvalue of generated\nCommunica-\ntionGroupServer\nservice shall be the\nSHORT-NAME\nof the according Communi-\ncation Group\ntemplate\nconcatenated by the name\nServer\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_-\nCM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99022]\n{OBSOLETE}\nSHORT-NAME\nvalue of generated\nCommunica-\ntionGroupClient\nservice\nd\nThe\nSHORT-NAME\nvalue of generated\nCommunica-\ntionGroupClient\nservice shall be the\nSHORT-NAME\nof the according Communi-\ncation Group\ntemplate\nconcatenated by the name\nClient\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_-\nCM_00601)\nThe figures below outline the Communication Group creation flow.\nThe Communication Group\nTemplate\ndefines the name of the Communication Group\nand defines the\nmessage\nand\nmessage response\ndatatypes."

It\nis used with an\nInstanceSpecifier\nand shall be specified as followed:\n<port context>::<port name>\n, where:\n\u000f\n<port context>\nspecifies the instantiation context of the port which might be\nan instantiation path or any other unique identifiable information.\n\u000f\n<port name>\nspecifies the port name.\nNote: it is possible to specify multiple technology bindings for a port (Multi-Binding).\nc\n(RS_CM_00200, RS_AP_00137)\n[SWS_CM_10416]\n{DRAFT}\nReception of a malformed message\nd\nIn case any net-\nwork binding does receive a message, which it identifies as malformed, the message\nshall be discarded and the error shall not be propagated to the application.\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00005)\nNote: The incident should also be logged if logging is configured and the corresponding\nnetwork binding supports it.\n7.4.1 SOME/IP Network binding\nSOME/IP supports different kind of bindings:\nSOME/IP Events:\n\u000f\nuni-cast is one-to-one communication\n\u000f\nmulti-cast is one-to-many communication\n72 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "source_page": 73,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nIn case the active subscriptions will reach the multi-cast-threshold the communication\nparadigm will be switched from uni-cast to multi-cast to gain a better network utilization.\nBelow the multi-cast-threshold\nSOME/IP\nis maintaining for a subscription a single uni-\ncast communication.\nSOME/IP Events:\n\u000f\nmany-to-one communication using multiple uni-cast communications\n[SWS_CM_10000] SOME/IP Compliance\nd\nThe SOME/IP network binding shall imple-\nment the SOME/IP Protocol and the SOME/IP Service Discovery Protocol defined in\n[4] and [6].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00205)\nThe byte order of the SOME/IP header fields is defined as network byte order by\n[PRS_SOMEIP_00368].\nThe byte order of addtional fields in the SOME/IP payload is defined as network byte\norder by [PRS_SOMEIP_00759].\n[SWS_CM_10172] Payload Byte order definition\nd\nThe byte order of the parame-\nters inside the payload shall be defined according to [PRS_SOMEIP_00369] by\nby-\nteOrder\nof\nApSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00026)\n[SWS_CM_10240]\n{DRAFT}\nSession handling state\nd\nIn case of normal (i.e., non\nFire and Forget) method calls or getters and setters of\nFields\n(i.e., in case of\nSOME/IP messages of type REQUEST, RESPONSE, and ERROR) or if segmen-\ntation of SOME/IP messages needs to be performed (i.e. [SWS_CM_10454] and\n[SWS_CM_10455] and [SWS_CM_10456] apply and [SWS_CM_10457] does not ap-\nply) the Session handling shall be Active. Otherwise, the Session handling shall be\nInactive.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_SOMEIP_00012)\nNote: Segmentation of SOME/IP messages according to section 7.4.1.9.9.\n7.4.1.1 Static Service Connection\n[SWS_CM_02201] Static service connection\nd\nThe static connection of services\nwhich are bound to SOME/IP protocols shall be preformed by statically pre-configured\napplication end-points as described in the TPS_ManifestSpecification for a\nProvid-\nedSomeipServiceInstance\nby [TPS_MANI_03312], [TPS_MANI_03313] and for a\nRequiredSomeipServiceInstance\nby [TPS_MANI_03314], [TPS_MANI_03315],\n[TPS_MANI_03316].\nc\n(RS_CM_00710)\n[SWS_CM_02202] Service Discovery is bypassed by static service connection\nd\nThe service discovery protocols are bypassed in case of a static service connection.\nc\n()\n73 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_02203] Service versioning is not checked at runtime in case of a static\nservice connection\nd\nService versions are not checked at run-time in case of a static\nservice connection since the Service Discovery has been bypassed.\nc\n()\nNote: ara::com language APIs are agnostic to static service connection.\n7.4.1.2 Service Discovery\n7.4.1.2.1 Start of service discovery protocol\n[SWS_CM_11374] Periodic link state monitoring\nd\nThe SOME/IP network binding\nshall periodically monitor and obtain the current link state of the underlying network\ninterfaces.\nNote: This information is required since the behavior of SOME/IP service discovery is\ninfluenced by the current link state as well as by changes in the link state\nc\n()\n[SWS_CM_00201] Start of service discovery protocol on Server side\nd\nThe reg-\nistration of a new offered service which is bound to SOME/IP by invoking the\nOf-\nferService\nmethod (see [SWS_CM_00101]) of the\nServiceSkeleton\nclass shall\ntrigger the start of the initial wait phase of the SOME/IP service discovery protocol af-\nter link up according to [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00133].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00101,\nRS_SOMEIPSD_00024, RS_SOMEIPSD_00013)\nThe different phases of SOME/IP Service Discovery on the Server side are configured\nin the Manifest in the\nSomeipSdServerServiceInstanceConfig\nreferenced in\nProvidedSomeipServiceInstance\nelement in the role\nsdServerConfig\n. The\nconfiguration is described in more detail in TPS_ManifestSpecification by\n\u000f\n[TPS_MANI_03012] (Initial Wait Phase),\n\u000f\n[TPS_MANI_03013] (Repetition Phase),\n\u000f\n[TPS_MANI_03014] (Main Phase).\nThe corresponding timing parameters for these phases are configured via\nInitialS-\ndDelayConfig\nin the role\ninitialOfferBehavior\n,\nRequestResponseDelay\nin\nthe role\nrequestResponseDelay\n, and\nTimeValue\nin attribute\nofferCyclicDe-\nlay\n. The sharing of timers is described in [TPS_MANI_03230].\n[SWS_CM_00209] Start of service discovery protocol on Client side\nd\nWhen invok-\ning the\nFindService\nmethods (see [SWS_CM_00122] and [SWS_CM_00622]) or the\nStartFindService\nmethods (see [SWS_CM_00123] and [SWS_CM_00623]) of the\nServiceProxy\nclass, such a search request shall be considered as issuing an inter-\nnal service request as used in [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00435]. FindService shall not wait\nfor offer messages, but only check information available within the local AP-instance\n(StartFindService shall also not wait for offer messages as it only registers a handler).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00102, RS_SOMEIPSD_00024, RS_SOMEIPSD_00008)\n74 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "source_page": 85,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10389] Configuration of a data accumulation on a\nProvid-\nedSomeipServiceInstance\nfor transmission over UDP\nd\nFor a\nProvided-\nSomeipServiceInstance\nall\nmethod\nresponses and\nevent\ns for which the\nudp-\nCollectionTrigger\nis set to\nnever\nshall be aggregated in a buffer until a trigger\narrives that starts the data transmission.\nThe following trigger options shall be supported:\n\u000f\na SOME/IP message needs to be transmitted for which the\nudpCollection-\nTrigger\nis set to\nalways\n.\n\u000f\nthe\nudpCollectionBufferTimeout\nis reached for one of the SOME/IP mes-\nsage already aggregated in the buffer.\n\u000f\nthe buffer size defined by the attribute\nudpCollectionBufferSizeThresh-\nold\nis reached.\n\u000f\nadding the\nmethod\nresponse or\nevent\nto the buffer would lead to a message\nlarger than the maximum possible size (e.g. MTU size). In this case the actual\nbuffer shall be triggered before handling the new event or method response.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_10390] Configuration of a data accumulation on a\nRequired-\nSomeipServiceInstance\nfor transmission over UDP\nd\nFor a\nRequired-\nSomeipServiceInstance\nall\nmethod\nrequests for which the\nudpCollection-\nTrigger\nis set to\nnever\nshall be aggregated in a buffer until a trigger arrives that\nstarts the data transmission.\nThe following trigger options shall be supported:\n\u000f\na SOME/IP message needs to be transmitted for which the\nudpCollection-\nTrigger\nis set to\nalways\n.\n\u000f\nthe\nudpCollectionBufferTimeout\nis reached for one of the SOME/IP mes-\nsage already aggregated in the buffer.\n\u000f\nthe buffer size defined by the attribute\nudpCollectionBufferSizeThresh-\nold\nis reached.\n\u000f\nadding the\nmethod\nrequest or\nevent\nto the buffer would lead to a message\nlarger than the maximum possible size (e.g. MTU size). In this case the actual\nbuffer shall be triggered before handling the new event or method response.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\nIn the following sections the term \"sending of a SOME/IP message shall be requested\"\nwill be used to describe the fact that the sending of the message is requested but\nmay be deferred due to data accumulation for UDP data transmission according to\n[SWS_CM_10388], [SWS_CM_10389], and [SWS_CM_10390].\n85 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.1.4 Execution context of message reception actions\nIn the following sections the term \"upon reception\" will be used to describe the fact that\ncertain actions (e.g, the deserialization of the payload according to [SWS_CM_10294])\nwill be performed at a point in time between the actual reception of a message and\nthe call of the corresponding API (e.g., the\nGetNewSamples\n(see [SWS_CM_00701])\nmethod of the respective\nEvent\nclass). This specification deliberately does not explic-\nitly state whether these actions will be performed in the context of message reception,\nin the context of the API call, or in a completely seperate execution context to leave\nroom for potential optimizations of a concrete ara::com implementation.\nThe only restriction imposed here refers to the execution context of the\nEventRe-\nceiveHandler\n(see [SWS_CM_00309]).  Executing the\nEventReceiveHandler\nin the context of the\nGetNewSamples\n(see [SWS_CM_00701]) method is not allowed,\nsince according to [SWS_CM_00181] the\nEventReceiveHandler\nshall use the\nGet-\nNewSamples\nmethod to access the retrieved event data.\n[SWS_CM_11270]\n{DRAFT}\nSelecting elements of the ServiceInterface for SecOC\ntransmission\nd\nIt is possible to define which elements of the\nServiceInterface\nof\nthe particular\nAdaptivePlatformServiceInstance\nshall be securedby SecOC.\nThe selection of\nServiceInterface\nelements is done by the\nServiceInter-\nfaceElementSecureComConfig\nthat is aggregated by\nAdaptivePlatformSer-\nviceInstance\n.\nThe following configuration in the\nServiceInterfaceElementSecureComConfig\nis applicable:\n\u000f\nMethods\nThe roles\nmethodCall\nand\nmethodReturn\nidentify the\nmethod(s)\nthat shall\nbe sprotected by SecOC with the configuration settings that are available in the\nServiceInterfaceElementSecureComConfig\nelement.\n\u000f\nEvents\nThe role\nevent\nidentifies the\nevent(s)\nthat shall be protected by SecOC\nwith the configuration settings that are availble in the\nServiceInterfaceEle-\nmentSecureComConfig\nelement.\n\u000f\nFields\nThe roles\nfieldNotifier\n,\ngetterCall\n,\ngetterReturn\n,\nsetterCall\nand\nsetterReturn\nidentify the\nfield\ncontent that shall be protected by SecOC\nwith the configuration settings that are available in the\nServiceInterfaceEle-\nmentSecureComConfig\nelement.\nc\n(RS_CM_00801, RS_CM_00803)\n86 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.1.5 Handling Events\n[SWS_CM_10287] Conditions for sending of a SOME/IP event message\nd\nThe\nsending of a SOME/IP event message shall be requested by invoking the\nSend\nmethod\nof the respective\nEvent\nclass (see [SWS_CM_00162] and [SWS_CM_90437])\n\u000f\nIf there is static service connection according to [SWS_CM_02201]\n\u000f\nIf there is at least one active subscriber and the offer of the service containing the\nevent has not been stopped (either because the TTL contained in the SOME/IP\nOfferService message (see [SWS_CM_00203]) has expired or because the\nStopOfferService\nmethod (see [SWS_CM_00111]) of the\nServiceSkele-\nton\nclass has been called).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, the transport proto-\ncol defined via the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n.\neventDeployment\n.\ntransportProtocol\nattribute (see [TPS_MANI_03050]).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_-\nCM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_00010)\n[SWS_CM_10289] Source of a SOME/IP event message\nd\nThe SOME/IP event mes-\nsage shall use the unicast IP address and port taken from the IPv4/v6 Endpoint Option\n(see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00307] and [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00315]) of the SOME/IP Of-\nferService message ([SWS_CM_00203]) or the server address which has been stat-\nically pre-configured by the static service connection according to [SWS_CM_02201]\nas source address and source port for the transmission.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_00042)\n[SWS_CM_10290] Destination of a SOME/IP event message\nd\nThe SOME/IP event\nmessage shall use the multicast IP address and the port taken from the IPv4/v6 Mul-\nticast Option (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00326] and [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00333]) destination address and destination port for the\ntransmission if the threshold defined by the\nmulticastThreshold\nattribute of the\nSomeipProvidedEventGroup\nthat is aggregated by the\nProvidedSomeipServi-\nceInstance\nin the role\neventGroup\nin the Manifest has been reached (see [PRS_-\nSOMEIPSD_00134]). The SOME/IP event message shall use the unicast IP ad-\ndress and the port taken from the IPv4/v6 Endpoint Option (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_-\n00307] and [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00315]) of the SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup mes-\nsage ([SWS_CM_00205]) as destination address and destination port for the transmis-\nsion if this threshold has not been reached (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00134]). In case\nmultiple Endpoint Options have been contained in the SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup\nmessage, the one matching the selected transport protocol (see [SWS_CM_10289])\nshall be used.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00042)\n87 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10291] Content of the SOME/IP event message\nd\nThe entries in the\nSOME/IP event message shall be as follows:\n\u000f\nThe Service ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) shall be derived from the Manifest\nwhere the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nser-\nviceInterfaceId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) shall be derived from the Mani-\nfest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\neventDeployment\n.\neventId\nby adding 0x8000 to the\neventDeployment\n.\neventId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Length (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00042]) shall be set to the length of the seri-\nalized payload in units of bytes incremented by 8 (second part of the SOME/IP\nheader that is covered by the Length)\n\u000f\nThe Client ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00702]) is unused for event messages (ac-\ncording to [PRS_SOMEIP_00702]) and thus shall be set to 0x0000.\n\u000f\nIn case of inactive Session Handling, see [SWS_CM_10240], the Session ID (see\n[PRS_SOMEIP_00703]) is unused for event messages and thus shall be set to\n0x0000 (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00932]) and [PRS_SOMEIP_00925]).\nIn case of active Session Handling, see [SWS_CM_10240], the Session ID\nis used for event messages and thus shall be incremented (with proper wrap\naround) upon every transmission of an event message (see [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00933], [PRS_SOMEIP_00934], [PRS_SOMEIP_00521], and [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00925]).\n\u000f\nThe Protocol Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00052]) shall be set to 0x01.\n\u000f\nThe Interface Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00053]) shall be derived from the\nManifest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines\nthe\nserviceInterfaceVersion\n.\nmajorVersion\n.\n\u000f\nThe Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) shall be set to\nNOTIFICATION\n(0x02).\n\u000f\nThe Return Code (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00058] and [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) is\nunused for event messages and thus (according to [PRS_SOMEIP_00925]) shall\nbe set to\nE_OK\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nThe Payload shall contain the serialized payload (i.e., the serialized\nVariable-\nDataPrototype\ncomposed by the\nServiceInterface\nin role\nevent\n) accord-\ning to the SOME/IP serialization rules.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00041, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00022, RS_SOMEIP_00003, RS_SOMEIP_00004)\nThe serialization rules\nare explained in section 7.4.1.9.\n[SWS_CM_10292] Checks for a received SOME/IP event message\nd\nUpon reception\nof a SOME/IP event message the following checks shall be conducted:\n88 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nIn case multiple Endpoint Options have been contained in the SOME/IP OfferService\nmessage, the one matching the selected transport protocol (see [SWS_CM_10298])\nshall be used.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00006, RS_SOMEIP_00007)\n[SWS_CM_10301] Content of the SOME/IP request message\nd\nThe entries in the\nSOME/IP request message shall be as follows:\n\u000f\nThe Service ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) shall be derived from the Manifest\nwhere the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nser-\nviceInterfaceId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) shall be derived from the Mani-\nfest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nmethodDeployment\n.\nmethodId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Length (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00042]) shall be set to the length of the seri-\nalized payload in units of bytes incremented by 8 (second part of the SOME/IP\nheader that is covered by the Length)\n\u000f\nThe Client ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00702]) shall be set to a value that uniquely\nidentifies the client within a\nMachine\n. - This may be achived by dynamically\ngenerating unique client IDs upon construction of the\nServiceProxy\n.\n\u000f\nThe Session ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00703]) shall be set to 0x0001 for the first\ncall of a particular method by a given client and shall be incremented by 1 af-\nter each call performed by this client for the respective method (see [PRS_-\nSOMEIP_00533]). Once the Session ID reaches 0xFFFF, it shall wrap around\nand start with 0x0001 again (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00521]).\n\u000f\nThe Protocol Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00052]) shall be set to 0x01.\n\u000f\nThe Interface Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00053]) shall be derived from the\nManifest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines\nthe\nserviceInterfaceVersion\n.\nmajorVersion\n.\n\u000f\nThe Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) shall be set to\nRE-\nQUEST_NO_RETURN\n(0x01) in case the\nClientServerOperation\nreferenced\nby\nmethodDeployment\n.\nmethod\ncontains a\nfireAndForget\nattribute which is\nset to\ntrue\n. The Message Type shall be set to\nREQUEST\n(0x00) otherwise.\n\u000f\nThe Return Code (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00058] and [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) is\nunused for request messages and thus (according to [PRS_SOMEIP_00920])\nshall be set to\nE_OK\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nThe Payload shall contain the serialized payload (i.e., the\nArgumentDataPro-\ntotype\ns of the\nClientServerOperation\nwith\ndirection\nset to\nin\nand\ninout\nserialized according to their order) according to the SOME/IP serialization\nrules.\n94 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

Verify that the Message Type is set to\nREQUEST\n(0x00) otherwise.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Interface Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00053]) matches\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n.\nserviceInterfaceVersion\n.\nmajorVersion\n.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Return Code (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00058] and [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00191]) is set to\nE_OK\n(0x00).\nIf any of the above checks fails the received SOME/IP request mes-\nsage shall be discarded and the incident shall be logged (if logging is\nenabled for the\nara::com\nimplementation).       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10332] Destination of a SOME/IP request message\nd\nThe destination ad-\ndress and the destination port of the SOME/IP request message shall be set accord-\ning to [SWS_CM_10300].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10333] Content of the SOME/IP request message\nd\nThe entries in the\nSOME/IP request message shall be as follows:\n\u000f\nThe Service ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) shall be derived from the Manifest\nwhere the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nser-\nviceInterfaceId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) for the\nSet\nmethod shall be derived\nfrom the Manifest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement\ndefines the\nfieldDeployment\n.\nset\n.\nmethodId\n. The Method ID for the\nGet\nmethod shall be derived from the Manifest where the\nSomeipServiceInter-\nfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nfieldDeployment\n.\nget\n.\nmethodId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Length (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00042]) shall be set to the length of the seri-\nalized payload in units of bytes incremented by 8 (second part of the SOME/IP\nheader that is covered by the Length)\n\u000f\nThe Client ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00702]) shall be set to a value that uniquely\nidentifies the client within a\nMachine\n.  This may be achieved by dynamically\ngenerating unique client IDs upon construction of the\nServiceProxy\n.\n\u000f\nThe Session ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00703]) shall be set to 0x0001 for the first\ncall of the particular method by a given client and shall be incremented by 1\nafter each call performed by this client for the respective method (see [PRS_-\nSOMEIP_00533]). Once the Session ID reaches 0xFFFF, it shall wrap around\nand start with 0x0001 again (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00521]).\n\u000f\nThe Protocol Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00052]) shall be set to 0x01.\n\u000f\nThe Interface Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00053]) shall be derived from the\nManifest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines\nthe\nserviceInterfaceVersion\n.\nmajorVersion\n.\n\u000f\nThe Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) shall be set to\nREQUEST\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nThe Return Code (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00058] and [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) is\nunused for request messages and thus (according to [PRS_SOMEIP_00920])\nshall be set to\nE_OK\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nThe Payload for the request message for the\nSet\nmethod shall contain the seri-\nalized payload (i.e., the serialized\nField\ncomposed by the\nServiceInterface\nin role\nfield\n) according to the SOME/IP serialization rules. The Payload for the\nrequest message for the\nGet\nmethod will be empty.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218, RS_SOMEIP_00003,\n106 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nRS_SOMEIP_00012, RS_SOMEIP_00021, RS_SOMEIP_00025, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00041)\nThe SOME/IP serialization rules are explained in section 7.4.1.9.\n[SWS_CM_10334] Checks for a received SOME/IP request message\nd\nUpon recep-\ntion of a SOME/IP request message the following checks shall be conducted:\n\u000f\nVerify that the Protocol Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00052]) is set to 0x01.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Length (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00042]) is larger than 7.\n\u000f\nUse the Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) which is set to\nREQUEST\n(0x00) to determine that the received SOME/IP message is actually a SOME/IP\nrequest message.\n\u000f\nUse the Service ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) and the\nserviceInter-\nfaceId\nattribute of the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement in\nthe Manifest to determine the right\nServiceInterface\n.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) matches the\nmetho-\ndId\nattribute of one of the\nSomeipMethodDeployment\ns of the\nSomeipSer-\nviceInterfaceDeployment\n.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) is set to\nREQUEST\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nVerify that the Interface Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00053]) matches\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n.\nserviceInterfaceVersion\n.\nmajorVersion\n.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Return Code (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00058] and [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00191]) is set to\nE_OK\n(0x00).\nIf any of the above checks fails the received SOME/IP request mes-\nsage shall be discarded and the incident shall be logged (if logging is\nenabled for the\nara::com\nimplementation). In case of a received RE-\nQUEST message (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]), additionally, an ERROR\nmessage with return code set to either\nE_WRONG_PROTOCOL_VERSION\n,\nE_UNKNOWN_SERVICE\n,\nE_WRONG_INTERFACE_VERSION\n,\nE_UNKNOWN_METHOD\n,\nor\nE_WRONG_MESSAGE_TYPE\n(see [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the\nrequester, depending on the detected error.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200,\nRS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00003, RS_SOMEIP_00019, RS_SOMEIP_00021, RS_SOMEIP_00008,\nRS_SOMEIP_00014)\n[SWS_CM_10335] Identifying the right method\nd\nUsing the Service ID (see [PRS_-\nSOMEIP_00245]) and the\nserviceInterfaceId\nattribute of the\nSomeipServi-\nceInterfaceDeployment\nelement as well as the Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00245]) and the\nmethodId\nattribute of the\nSomeipFieldDeployment\n.\nset\ns and\nSomeipFieldDeployment\n.\nget\ns of the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n,\n107 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_11263] Precedence of alignment settings for a variable data length\ndata element\nd\nIf\nSomeipDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTrans-\nformationProps\n.\nalignment\nand\nTransformationPropsToServiceInter-\nfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nalignment\nare both not set for a\nvariable data length data element, no alignment shall be applied.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204,\nRS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10263] Padding for a fixed length data element\nd\nAfter serialized fixed\ndata length data elements, the SOME/IP network binding shall never add automatically\na padding for alignment.\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00211)\nNote:\nIf the following data element shall be aligned, a padding element of according size\nneeds to be explicitly inserted into the\nCppImplementationDataType\n.\n[SWS_CM_10037] Alignment calculation\nd\nAlignment shall always be calculated from\nstart of SOME/IP message.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_-\nCM_00211)\nThis attribute defines the memory alignment. The SOME/IP network binding does not\ntry to automatically align parameters but aligns as specified. The alignment is currently\nconstraint to multiple of 1 Byte to simplify code generators.\nSOME/IP payload should be placed in memory so that the SOME/IP payload is suit-\nable aligned. For infotainment ECUs an alignment of 8 Bytes (i.e. 64 bits) should be\nachieved, for all ECU at least an alignment of 4 Bytes should be achieved. An efficient\nalignment is highly hardware dependent.\n[SWS_CM_10016] Deserializing of exceeded unexpected data\nd\nIf more data than\nexpected shall be deserialized, the unexpected data shall be discarded. The known\nfraction shall be considered.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00202)\n[SWS_CM_11411] Deserializing incomplete data on the skeleton side\nd\nIf less\ndata than expected shall be deserialized on the skeleton side the data shall be dis-\ncarded and the incident shall be logged. In case of a received REQUEST mes-\nsage (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]), additionally, an ERROR message with return code\nset to\nE_MALFORMED_MESSAGE\n(see [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the re-\nquester.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00202)\n[SWS_CM_11412] Deserializing incomplete data on the proxy side\nd\nIf less data\nthan expected shall be deserialized on the proxy side and the data to be deserialized\ndoes not belong to a Field or Event, the data shall be discarded and the incident shall\nbe logged. In case of a received REQUEST message (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]),\nadditionally, an ERROR message with return code set to\nE_MALFORMED_MESSAGE\n(see [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the requester.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_-\nCM_00202)\n[SWS_CM_10017] Deserializing incomplete data on the proxy side belonging to\na field and initValue defined\nd\nIf less data than expected shall be deserialized on the\nproxy side and the data to be deserialized belong to a\nField\nand the\ninitValue\nis\n112 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nNote: Primitive\nStdCppImplementationDataType\ns defined in [14].\nThe Byte Order is specified common for all parameters by\nbyteOrder\nof\nApSomeip-\nTransformationProps\n.\n7.4.1.9.2 Enumeration Data Types\n[SWS_CM_10361] Serializing Enumeration Data Type\nd\nEnumeration Data\nType\nshall be serialized according to [SWS_CM_10036] based on their underlying\nprimitive\nStdCppImplementationDataType\n(i.e., the\nPrimitive Cpp Imple-\nmentation Data Type\nthat is defined as the underlying type of the enumeration\nas defined in [SWS_LBAP_00027])\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211)\n7.4.1.9.3 Structured Data Types (structs)\n[SWS_CM_10042] Serializing a struct Data Type\nd\nA\nStructure Cpp Implemen-\ntation Data Type\nshall be serialized in order of depth-first traversal.\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\nThe SOME/IP network binding doesn't automatically align parameters of a struct.\nInsert reserved/padding elements into the AUTOSAR data type if needed for alignment,\nsince the SOME/IP network binding shall not automatically add such padding.\nSo if for example a struct includes a std::uint8_t and a std::uint32_t, they are just written\nsequentially into the buffer. This means that there is no padding between the uint8\nand the first byte of the std::uint32_t; therefore, the std::uint32_t might not be aligned.\nSo the system designer has to consider to add padding elements to the data type to\nachieve the required alignment or set it globally.\nWarning about unaligned structs or similar shall not be done in the SOME/IP network\nbinding but only in the tool chain used to generate the SOME/IP network binding.\nThe SOME/IP network binding does not automatically insert dummy/padding elements.\nSOME/IP allows to add a length field of 8, 16 or 32 bit in front of structs. The length\nfield of a struct describes the number of bytes of the struct. This allows for extensible\nstructs which allow better migration of interfaces.\n[SWS_CM_00252] Missing size of length field for structs\nd\nIf attribute\nSomeip-\nDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransformationProps\n.\nsize-\nOfStructLengthField\nis set to a value equal to 0, no length field shall be inserted\nin front of the serialized struct for which the\nApSomeipTransformationProps\nis\ndefined via\nSomeipDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransfor-\nmationProps\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n114 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "source_page": 118,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.1.9.4 Structured Datatypes and Arguments with Identifier and optional\nMembers\nTo achieve enhanced forward and backward compatibility, an additional Data ID can\nbe added in front of struct members or method arguments. The receiver then can\nskip unknown members/arguments, i.e. where the Data ID is unknown. New member-\ns/arguments can be added at arbitrary positions when Data IDs are transferred in the\nserialized byte stream.\nStructs are modeled in the Manifest using\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory\nSTRUCTURE\nand members are represented by\nCppImplementation-\nDataTypeElement\ns. Method arguments are represented by ArgumentDataProto-\ntypes.\nThe assignment of Data IDs is modeled in the Manifest in the context of\nTransforma-\ntionPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n. Refer to [5] for more details.\nMoreover, the usage of Data IDs allows describing structs with optional members.\nWhether a member is optional or not, is defined in the Manifest using the attribute\nCppImplementationDataTypeElement\n.\nisOptional\n.\nWhether an optional member is actually present in the struct or not, is to be determined\nduring runtime. This is realized in the Adaptive Platform using the\nara::core::\nOptional\nclass template (see 8.1.2.6.3 Optional Data Types).\nIn addition to the Data ID, a wire type encodes the datatype of the following member.\nData ID and wire type are encoded in a so-called tag.\nFor more details, please refer to [4].\n[SWS_CM_90443] Wire type for non-dynamic data types\nd\nIf\nTransforma-\ntionPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nisDynamicLengthFieldSize\nis set to false or is not defined, the serializer\nshall use wire type 4 for serializing complex types and shall use the fixed size\nlength fields. The size is defined in\nTransformationPropsToServiceInter-\nfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nsizeOfStructLengthField\n,\nsizeOfArrayLengthField\nor\nsizeOfStringLengthField\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_90444] Wire type for dynamic data types\nd\nIf\nTransformationProp-\nsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nisDynami-\ncLengthFieldSize\nis set to true, the transformer shall use wire types 5,6,7 for\nserializing complex types and shall chose the size of the length field according to this\nwire type.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_90445] A deserializer shall always be able to handle the wire types\n4, 5, 6 and 7\nd\nA deserializer shall always be able to handle the wire types 4, 5, 6\nand 7 independent of the setting of\nTransformationPropsToServiceInter-\nfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nisDynamicLengthFieldSize\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\n118 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P119_277",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_90446",

      "source_page": 119,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_90446] Data ID\nd\nIf a Data ID is defined for an\nArgumentDataPrototype\nor\nCppImplementationDataType\nby means of\nTransformationPropsToSer-\nviceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\nTlvDataIdDefinition\n.\nid\n, a tag shall be in-\nserted in the serialized byte stream.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\nNote: regarding existence of Data IDs, refer to [5].\nNote: regarding existence of length field, refer to [4].\nRationale: The length field is required to skip unknown members/arguments during\ndeserialization.\n[SWS_CM_90451] Byte order for the length field of serialized structs\nd\nTransfor-\nmationPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nshall define the byte order for the length field.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_90452] Default byte order for the length field of structs\nd\nIf\nTransformationPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransfor-\nmationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nis not defined, a byte order of mostSignificantByteFirst\nshall be used for the length field.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\nRegarding structure members and serialization examples, refer to [4].\n7.4.1.9.5 Strings\n[SWS_CM_10053] Strings encoding\nd\nStrings shall be encoded using Unicode and\nterminated with a \"\\0\"-character.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10054] Supported encoding\nd\nDifferent Unicode encoding shall be sup-\nported including UTF-8, UTF-16BE, and UTF-16LE. Since these encoding have a dy-\nnamic length of bytes per character, the maximum length in bytes is up to three times\nthe length of characters in UTF-8 plus 1 Byte for the termination with a \"\\0\" or two\ntimes the length of the characters in UTF-16 plus 2 Bytes for a \"\\0\". UTF-8 character\ncan be up to 6 bytes and an UTF-16 character can be up to 4 bytes.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204,\nRS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211, RS_AP_00136)\n[SWS_CM_10285] Responsibility of proper string encoding\nd\nThe application pro-\nvides the string always in the UTF-8 encoding. The SOME/IP binding has to re-\nencode the data to the on-the-wire encoding that is configured by\nApSomeipTrans-\nformationProps\n.\nstringEncoding\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_-\n00202, RS_CM_00211, RS_AP_00136)\n[SWS_CM_10055] UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE terminating bytes\nd\nUTF-16LE and\nUTF-16BE strings shall be zero terminated with a \"\\0\" character. This means they shall\nend with (at least) two 0x00 Bytes.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211)\n119 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nNote: If\nburstSize\nis set on receiver side it can be used to optimize buffer handling\nfor reception of bursts.\n7.4.1.10 Marker Interface\nOn the AUTOSAR adaptive platform there are use-cases for the utilization of a Servi-\nceInterface that does not have any method, event, or field defined. In other words, the\nexistence of a ServiceInterface by itself represents a valid semantics that has a value\non its own.\nA service instance that corresponds to such a ServiceInterface may be offered with the\nmere intention to signal that the ECU that provides the service instance is becoming\nready for something. So the SOME/IP Service Discovery mechanism is used to indi-\ncate the readiness. But for the communication not SOME/IP but a different protocol will\nbe used.\nFor example an ECU may indicate with a service offer that it is ready to being diag-\nnosed. A tester could then take the existence of the offer as an indication to initiate a\nconnection to the respective ECU.\n[SWS_CM_10458] Handling of an ServiceInterface that does not contain any\nevents, methods, or fields\nd\nIf a\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nis de-\nfined for a ServiceInterface that does not contain any events, methods, or fields and\na\nProvidedSomeipServiceInstance\nis defined in the\nServiceInstanceMani-\nfest\nthat points to the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nin the role servi-\nceInterface then:\n\u000f\nthe ServiceInterface shall be offered over SOME/IP as defined by\n[SWS_CM_00203] which means that the Endpoint Option shall include\nthe IP-Address, Port Number and Protocol as defined by the\nProvided-\nSomeipServiceInstance\n\u000f\nthe Server shall not create a UDP/TCP socket and shall not bind any socket to\nthe configured server address\nc\n(RS_CM_00101)\n7.4.2 Signal-Based Network binding\nThe applications on the adaptive platform communicate with each other in a service-\noriented manner. When exchanging information with software components executed\non an AUTOSAR classic platform which make use of signal-based communication,\na conversion between this signal-based communication and the service-oriented com-\nmunication needs to take place. Hereby the signals of a received signal-based commu-\nnication is being made available as elements of a provided\nServiceInterface\n. The\nsignals of a sent signal-based communication are being made available as elements of\n134 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\na required\nServiceInterface\n. The conversion between signal-based communica-\ntion and service-oriented communication may be performed by a software component\non an AUTOSAR classic platform gateway ECU or by an adaptive application on an\nAUTOSAR adaptive platform\nMachine\n.\nThere are two approaches how the signal-based information is made available at the\nadaptive AUTOSAR\nMachine\n:\n\u000f\nNetwork binding (see section 7.4.2.1)\n\u000f\nNetwork binding (see section 7.4.2.2)\n7.4.2.1 Signal-Based SOME/IP Network binding\nThe\nSignal-Based SOME/IP\nnetwork binding is currently a specialization of the\nSOME/IP\nnetwork binding and many aspects of the\nSOME/IP\nnetwork binding are\nre-used. Instead of replicating many specification items from the\nSOME/IP\nnetwork\nbinding the approach of this\nSignal-Based SOME/IP\nnetwork binding chapter is to\nreplicate the chapter structure. Specification items which are applicable to the\nSig-\nnal-Based SOME/IP\nnetwork binding are just referenced, specification items which\nare NOT applicable to the\nSignal-Based SOME/IP\nnetwork binding are explicitly ex-\ncluded (via reference), and changed specification items are marked and the origin is\nreferenced.\nOne major difference between the SOME/IP network binding and the\nSignal-Based\nSOME/IP\nnetwork binding is the serialization technology. While the SOME/IP network\nbinding only supports SOME/IP serialized payload the\nSignal-Based SOME/IP\nnet-\nwork binding supports the signal-based serialization of Classic platform COM-Stack as\nwell as the SOME/IP serialization of payload (in order to support mixed use-cases).\n[SWS_CM_11269]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of serialization technology\nd\nThe serialization\ntechnology is defined by the attribute\nSomeipEventDeployment\n.\nserializer\n. If the\nattribute is set to\nsignalBased\nthen the signal-service-translation is responsible for\nthe handling of the serialization. If the attribute is set to\nsomeip\nthen the SOME/IP\nserializer is responsible for the handling of the serialization.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\nSee also chapter 7.4.2.1.8 and chapter 7.4.1.9.\nIn figure 7.16 an example of a mixed serialized service is illustrated. The event\nx\nis\ndefined to use\nsomeip serializer\nwhile event\ny\nis defined to use\nsignalBased\nserializer\n.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.2.2 Signal-Based Static Network binding\nThe\nSignal-Based Static\nnetwork binding is enabled when a\nService-\nInstanceToSignalMapping\nrefers to a\nProvidedUserDefinedServiceIn-\nstance\nor\nRequiredUserDefinedServiceInstance\nof\ncategory SIGNAL-\nBASED_WITH_HEADER\nor\nSIGNALBASED_NO_HEADER\n.\nPlease note that there is currently no static\nara::com\nAPI optimization defined, thus\nit is expected that the adaptive application, which interacts with a\nServiceInter-\nface\n, uses the same steps as in any other service oriented interaction (i.e. calling\nOfferService(), FindService(), Subscribe(), ...).\nThe general approach is:\nFor a\nProvidedUserDefinedServiceInstance\nthe connection is established in a\nUDP / TCP Server role.\nFor a\nRequiredUserDefinedServiceInstance\nthe connection is established in a\nUDP / TCP Client role.\n7.4.2.2.1 Service Discovery\n[SWS_CM_80501]\n{DRAFT}\nMapping of Offer Service (\nSignal-Based Static\nnetwork binding)\nd\nWhen instructed to\noffer\na service instance which is\nmapped to a\nProvidedUserDefinedServiceInstance\nof\ncategory SIGNAL-\nBASED_WITH_HEADER\nor\nSIGNALBASED_NO_HEADER\n, then the\nSignal-Based\nStatic\nnetwork binding shall create / use a socket for each entry in the\nremotePeers\nlist. Each connection is defined by the\nlocalUdpPortNumber\nor\nlocalTcpPort-\nNumber\nand one element out of the\nremotePeers\nlist. If a connection with identical\ncredentials already exists then this existing connection shall be used.\nIf a\nlocalUdpPortNumber\nis defined then each connection is created using the UDP\nprotocol and bound to the listed\nremotePeers\n.\nIf a\nlocalTcpPortNumber\nis defined then each connection is created using the TCP\nprotocol and is listening for client connections.\nc\n(RS_CM_00004, RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_80512]\n{DRAFT}\nMapping of Stop Offer Service (\nSignal-Based\nStatic\nnetwork binding)\nd\nWhen instructed to\nstop offering\na service instance which\nis mapped to a\nProvidedUserDefinedServiceInstance\nof\ncategory SIG-\nNALBASED_WITH_HEADER\nor\nSIGNALBASED_NO_HEADER\n, then the\nSignal-Based\nStatic\nnetwork binding shall check:\n\u000f\nIf this is the last service instance which uses the respective connection then this\nconnection shall be closed.\n\u000f\nIf there are still other service instance using this connection then the connection\nshall be kept open.\nc\n(RS_CM_00004, RS_CM_00204)\n153 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.2.2.2 Accumulation of messages\n[SWS_CM_80505]\n{DRAFT}\nData accumulation for UDP data transmission (\nSignal-Based Static\nnetwork binding)\nd\nTo allow for the transmission of multi-\nple messages (signal-based events and signal-based field notifiers) within a single\nUDP datagram, data accumulation for UDP data transmission shall be supported.\nc\n(RS_CM_00004, RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_80504]\n{DRAFT}\nConfiguration of a data accumulation on a\nRequire-\ndUserDefinedServiceInstance\nfor transmission over UDP (\nSignal-Based\nStatic\nnetwork binding)\nd\nFor a\nProvidedUserDefinedServiceInstance\nof\ncategory SIGNALBASED_WITH_HEADER\nwhich has a\nudpCollectionBuffer-\nSizeThreshold\n> 0 defined, the events and field notifiers where\nudpCollection-\nTrigger\nis set to\nnever\nshall be aggregated in a buffer until a trigger arrives that\nstarts the data transmission.\nThe following trigger options shall be supported:\n\u000f\na message needs to be transmitted for which the\nudpCollectionTrigger\nis\nset to\nalways\n.\n\u000f\nthe\nudpCollectionBufferTimeout\nis reached for one of the messages al-\nready aggregated in the buffer.\n\u000f\nthe buffer size defined by the attribute\nudpCollectionBufferSizeThresh-\nold\nis reached.\n\u000f\nadding the event of field notifier to the buffer would lead to a message larger than\nthe maximum possible size (e.g. MTU size). In this case the actual buffer shall\nbe triggered before handling the new event or field notifier.\nc\n(RS_CM_00004, RS_CM_00204)\n7.4.2.2.3 Execution context of message reception actions\nThe section 7.4.1.4 is fully applicable to the\nSignal-Based Static\nnetwork binding.\n7.4.2.2.4 Handling Events\n[SWS_CM_80506]\n{DRAFT}\nArbitrary Message Header\nusage for\nSignal-\nBased Static\nnetwork binding messages\nd\nIf a\nProvidedUserDefinedSer-\nviceInstance\nor\nRequiredUserDefinedServiceInstance\nof\ncategory SIG-\nNALBASED_WITH_HEADER\nis defined then each message shall have an\nArbitrary\nMessage Header\n(see [TPS_Manifest]) defined. This message header is composed\nof a 32 bit wide Message ID field and 32 bit wide Message Length field. Both encoded\nin big endian.\n155 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe the signal based payload is appended (the Message Length field is used to deter-\nmine how long the payload is in bytes).\nc\n(RS_CM_00004, RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_80507]\n{DRAFT}\nNo header option for\nSignal-Based Static\nnetwork\nbinding messages\nd\nIf a\nProvidedUserDefinedServiceInstance\nor\nRequire-\ndUserDefinedServiceInstance\nof\ncategory SIGNALBASED_NO_HEADER\nis de-\nfined then there is no header information standardized and thus the signal based pay-\nload is the only content of the message.\nc\n(RS_CM_00004, RS_CM_00204)\n7.4.2.2.5 Handling Method Calls\n[SWS_CM_80508]\n{DRAFT}\nNo method support for\nSignal-Based Static\nnet-\nwork binding\nd\nThe\nSignal-Based Static\nnetwork binding does not support meth-\nods.\nc\n(RS_CM_00004, RS_CM_00204)\n7.4.2.2.6 Handling Fields\n[SWS_CM_80509]\n{DRAFT}\nOnly field notifier support for\nSignal-Based Static\nnetwork binding\nd\nThe\nSignal-Based Static\nnetwork binding only supports the\nfield notifier. Getter or Setter methods are not supported.\nc\n(RS_CM_00004, RS_CM_-\n00204)\n7.4.2.2.7 Serialization of Payload\nIn case of the static signal-service-translation always the signal-service-translation is\nresponsible for the handling of the serialization.\n[SWS_CM_80510]\n{DRAFT}\nIgnoring not mapped elements\nd\nTo allow migration the\ndeserialization shall ignore signals which are not subject to\nServiceInstance-\nToSignalMapping\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00004)\n[SWS_CM_80511]\n{DRAFT}\nDeserializing incomplete data belonging to a field\nd\nIf\nless data than expected shall be deserialized and the data to be deserialized belong\nto a\nField\n, the\ninitValue\nshall be used if it is defined. Otherwise the data shall\nbe completely discarded and the incident shall be logged (if logging is enabled for the\nara::com\nimplementation).\nc\n(RS_CM_00004)\n7.4.3 DDS Network binding\n[SWS_CM_11000] DDS Compliance\nd\nThe DDS network binding shall comply with the\nDDS Minimum Profile defined in [19], the DDS Wire Interoperability protocol (RTPS)\ndefined in [20], and the DDS-XTYPES Minimal Programming Interface and Network\nInteroperability Profiles defined in [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, FO_RS_Dds_00001)\n156 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "source_page": 157,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_90500]\n{DRAFT}\nChoice of Service Instance discovery protocol\nd\nDdsProvidedServiceInstance\ns and\nDdsRequiredServiceInstance\ns provide\na\ndiscoveryType\nattribute permitting the choice between two distinct discovery pro-\ntocols. For a Service Interface Skeleton to be discoverable by a Service Interface Proxy,\nboth shall be configured with the same\ndiscoveryType\nvalue.\nc\n(RS_CM_00101, RS_-\nCM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008)\nThe\nDomainParticipantUserDataQos\nsetting provides a discovery protocol that\nleverages the USER_DATA QoS policy of DDS Domain Participants, assigning a\npurpose-specific format string to it as described in 7.4.3.1 below. This approach is\nfast and nimble, since no additional DDS Entities beyond Domain Participants need to\nbe created to exercise discovery of Service Instances.\nThe\nTopic\nsetting provides, as described in section 7.4.3.2 below, a discovery proto-\ncol that employs a purpose-specific Topic of a well-defined type to distribute Service\nInstance announcements in a publish-subscribe, instance-based fashion. This pro-\ntocol, although more resource-demanding (DDS entities down to a single DataWriter\nneed to be created for Skeletons, same for a DataReader in Proxies), enhances in-\nteroperability and enables advanced DDS features such as persistence, routing and\ndurability.\n[SWS_CM_90501]\n{DRAFT}\nTopic naming for Domain Participant USER_DATA\nQoS - based Service Instances\nd\nWhen\nDomainParticipantUserDataQos\nis set in the\ndiscoveryType\nattribute for a specific\nDdsProvidedServi-\nceInstance\nor\nDdsRequiredServiceInstance\n, the de-facto Topic naming\nscheme for events, triggers, methods and fields is the one described for\nSER-\nVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_PARTITION\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00211, RS_-\nCM_00216, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00005)\n7.4.3.1 Service Discovery via Domain Participant USER_DATA QoS policy\n[SWS_CM_11001] Mapping of OfferService method\nd\nWhen instructed to offer a\nService, the DDS Binding shall perform the following operations:\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11002] It shall assign a DDS DomainParticipant to the Service In-\nstance.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11003] It shall assign a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to ev-\nery\nVariableDataPrototype\ndefined in the\nServiceInterface\nin the role\nevent\n.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_10550] It shall assign a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to every\nTrigger\ndefined in the\nServiceInterface\nin the role\ntrigger\n.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11029] It shall assign a DDS Request Topic and a DDS Reply Topic,\nand create their corresponding DDS DataWriter and DataReader, to provide ac-\ncess to all\nClientServerOperation\ns defined in the\nServiceInterface\nthe\nrole\nmethod\n.\n157 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
