      "source_page": 158,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11030] It shall assign a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to every\nField\ndefined in the\nServiceInterface\nin the role\nfield\nwith its\nhasNoti-\nfier\nattribute set to\ntrue\n.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11031] It shall assign a DDS Request Topic and a DDS Reply Topic,\nand create their corresponding DDS DataWriter and DDS DataReader, to provide\naccess to all the\nField\ns defined in the\nServiceInterface\nin the role\nfield\nwith\nhasGetter\nand/or\nhasSetter\nattributes set to\ntrue\nvia getter/setter invo-\ncation.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_09004] It shall add the Service ID, Service Instance IDs, and\nSer-\nviceInterface\ncontract version to the DDS DomainParticipant's USER_DATA\nQoS Policy.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00005)\n[SWS_CM_11002] Assigning a DDS DomainParticipant to a Service Instance\nd\nThe\nDDS Binding shall assign a DDS DomainParticipant to every Service Instance. The\nconfiguration of the DomainParticipant is described in the TPS_ManifestSpecification:\n\u000f\nThe Domain ID of the DomainParticipant shall be derived from the Manifest,\nwhere the\nDdsProvidedServiceInstance\nelement defines the\ndomainId\n.\n\u000f\nThe QoS Profile of the DomainParticipant shall be derived from the Manifest,\nwhere the\nDdsProvidedServiceInstance\nelement defines the\nqosProfile\n.\nBefore creating a new DomainParticipant, the DDS binding shall first look for existing\nDomainParticipants in the current process that match the configuration criteria speci-\nfied above\n3\n. If the search is successful, the binding shall assign the DomainParticipant\nfound to the Service\n4\n; otherwise, the binding shall create a new DomainParticipant\naccording to the desired configuration and assign it to the Service.\nOnce the DomainParticipant is available to the Service Instance, the binding implemen-\ntation shall create a DDS Publisher and a DDS Subscriber to enclose all DataWriters\nand DataReaders associated with the Instance. The Partition QoS of both the DDS\nPublisher and DDS Subscriber shall contain the following partition name:\n\"ara.com://services/<svcId>_<svcInId>\"\nWhere:\n<svcId>\nis the Service Id derived from the Manifest, where the\nDdsServiceInter-\nfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nserviceInterfaceId\n.\n<svcInId>\nis the Instance Id derived from the Manifest, where the\nDdsProvided-\nServiceInstance\nelement defines the\nserviceInstanceId\n."
    },

      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P159_321",

      "source_page": 159,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nPublisher and Subscriber objects may be reused across events and other resources\nprovided by the Service Instance; therefore, they shall not be removed until the enclos-\ning DomainParticipant is destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00005)\n[SWS_CM_11003] Assigning a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to every\nEvent in the ServiceInterface\nd\nThe DDS binding shall assign a DDS Topic to ev-\nery\nevent\nin the\nServiceInterface\naccording to the mapping rules specified in\n[SWS_CM_11015]. Since these DDS Topics may already be available in the Domain-\nParticipant assigned to the Service Instance (e.g., because a different Service Instance\nassigned to the same DomainParticipant may have created them), the service shall first\nlook for existing Topics in the DomainParticipant matching the required criteria. If the\nsearch is unsuccessful, the DomainParticipant shall create a new DDS Topic to repre-\nsent the\nevent\nas defined in [SWS_CM_11015].\nOnce all DDS Topics representing the\nevent\ns in the\nServiceInterface\nare ready\nfor use, the DomainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance shall create one DDS\nDataWriter of the equivalent Topic per\nevent\nusing the DDS Publisher created in\n[SWS_CM_11002]. The DataWriter shall be configured according to the\nqosProfile\nspecified in the associated\nDdsEventQosProps\n.\nTopic objects may be reused across service instances; therefore, they shall not be re-\nmoved until the enclosing DomainParticipant is destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00005, FO_RS_Dds_-\n00015)\n[SWS_CM_10550]\n{DRAFT}\nAssigning a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to ev-\nery Trigger in the ServiceInterface\nd\nThe DDS binding shall assign a DDS Topic to\nevery\ntrigger\nin the\nServiceInterface\naccording to the mapping rules specified\nin [SWS_CM_10524]. Since these DDS Topics may already be available in the Do-\nmainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance (e.g., because a different Service\nInstance assigned to the same DomainParticipant may have created them), the ser-\nvice shall first look for existing Topics in the DomainParticipant matching the required\ncriteria. If the search is unsuccessful, the DomainParticipant shall create a new DDS\nTopic to represent the\ntrigger\nas defined in [SWS_CM_10524].\nOnce all DDS Topics representing the\ntrigger\ns in the\nServiceInterface\nare\nready for use, the DomainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance shall create\none DDS DataWriter of the equivalent Topic per\ntrigger\nusing the DDS Publisher\ncreated in [SWS_CM_11002]. The DataWriter shall be configured according to the\nqosProfile\nspecified in the associated\nDdsEventQosProps\nthat in turn refers via\nDdsEventDeployment\nto the\ntrigger\ns.\nTopic objects may be reused across service instances; therefore, they shall not be re-\nmoved until the enclosing DomainParticipant is destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00005, FO_RS_Dds_-\n00015)\n159 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P160_322",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_11029",

      "source_page": 160,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_11029] Assigning a DDS Request and Reply Topic, and DataWriters\nand DataReaders, to the Methods in the ServiceInterface\nd\nThe DDS binding shall\ninstantiate a DDS Service [22] to handle requests to all the\nmethod\ns in the\nServi-\nceInterface\n.\nIn practice, this implies assigning a DDS Request Topic and a DDS Reply Topic to the\nDDS Service that handles those method calls according to the mapping rules spec-\nified in [SWS_CM_11100]. Since these DDS Topics may already be available in the\nDomainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance (e.g., because a different Service\nInstance assigned to the same DomainParticipant may have created them), the service\nshall first look for existing Topics in the DomainParticipant matching the required crite-\nria. If the search is unsuccessful, the DomainParticipant shall create new DDS Request\nand Reply Topics to represent the DDS Service as specified in [SWS_CM_11100].\nOnce the corresponding DDS Request and Reply Topics are ready for use, the Do-\nmainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance shall create:\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11106] A DDS DataReader of the DDS Request Topic to handle re-\nquests using the DDS Subscriber created in [SWS_CM_11002].\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11107] A DDS DataWriter of the DDS Reply Topic to handle replies\nusing the DDS Publisher created in [SWS_CM_11002].\nTopic objects may be reused across service instances; therefore, they shall not be\nremoved until the enclosing DomainParticipant is destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_-\nCM_00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00015)\nThe handling\nof method calls with DDS is specified in 7.4.3.5.\n[SWS_CM_11030] Assigning a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to every Field\nin the ServiceInterface with its hasNotifier attribute equal to true\nd\nThe DDS\nbinding shall assign a DDS Topic to every\nfield\nin the\nServiceInterface\nwith\nits\nhasNotifier\nattribute set to\ntrue\naccording to the mapping rules specified in\n[SWS_CM_11130]. Since these DDS Topics may already be available in the Domain-\nParticipant assigned to the Service Instance (e.g., because a different Service Instance\nassigned to the same DomainParticipant may have created them), the service shall first\nlook for existing Topics in the DomainParticipant matching the required criteria. If the\nsearch is unsuccessful, the DomainParticipant shall create a new DDS Topic to repre-\nsent the\nfield\nas defined in [SWS_CM_11130].\nOnce all DDS Topics representing the\nfield\ns in the\nServiceInterface\nare ready\nfor use, the DomainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance shall create one DDS\nDataWriter of the equivalent Topic per\nfield\nwith the\nhasNotifier\nattribute set to\ntrue\nusing the DDS Publisher created in [SWS_CM_11002]. The DataWriter shall\nbe configured according to the\nqosProfile\nspecified in the associated\nDdsField-\nQosProps\n.\nTopic objects may be reused across service instances; therefore, they shall not be re-\nmoved until the enclosing DomainParticipant is destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_-\n00015)\n160 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "source_page": 161,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_11031] Assigning a DDS Request and Reply Topic, and DataWriters\nand DataReaders, to the Field Getters/Setters in the ServiceInterface\nd\nThe DDS\nbinding shall instantiate a DDS Service [22] to handle get/set requests to all the\nfield\ns\nin the\nServiceInterface\nwith\nhasGetter\nand/or\nhasSetter\nset to\ntrue\n.\nIn practice, this implies assigning a DDS Request Topic and a DDS Reply Topic to the\nDDS Service according to the mapping rules specified in [SWS_CM_11144]. Since\nthese DDS Topics may already be available in the DomainParticipant assigned to the\nService Instance (e.g., because a different Service Instance assigned to the same Do-\nmainParticipant may have created them), the service shall first look for existing Topics\nin the DomainParticipant matching the required criteria. If the search is unsuccessful,\nthe DomainParticipant shall create new DDS Request and Reply Topics to represent\nthe DDS Service as specified in [SWS_CM_11144].\nOnce the corresponding DDS Request and Reply Topics are ready for use, the Do-\nmainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance shall create:\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11149] A DDS DataReader of the DDS Request Topic to handle re-\nquests using the DDS Subscriber created in [SWS_CM_11002].\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11150] A DDS DataWriter of the DDS Reply Topic to handle replies\nusing the DDS Publisher created in [SWS_CM_11002].\nTopic objects may be reused across service instances; therefore, they shall not be re-\nmoved until the enclosing DomainParticipant is destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_-\n00015, FO_RS_Dds_00016)\nThe handling of fields with DDS is specified in section\n7.4.3.6.\n[SWS_CM_09004] Adding Service IDs, Service Instance IDs, and ServiceInter-\nface Contract Versions to the DDS DomainParticipant's USER_DATA QoS Policy\nd\nThe binding implementation shall configure the USER_DATA QoS Policy of the DDS\nDomainParticipant associated with the Service Instance to propagate Service IDs, In-\nstance IDs, and\nServiceInterface\ncontract versions, using the native DDS discov-\nery mechanisms defined in [20]. The USER_DATA QoS Policy appends a user-defined\nvalue to the DomainParticipant's discovery messages. This information shall be used\nby ara::com Clients and DDS native applications to identify a DomainParticipant as an\nara::com DomainParticipant that provides one or more Service Instances.\nService IDs, Service Instance IDs, and\nServiceInterface\ncontract versions shall\nbe encoded in the USER_DATA QoS Policy in string format according to the following\npattern:\n\"ara.com://services/<svcId>_<svcInId>-<svcMajVersion>.<svcMinVersion>\n[&<svcId>_<svcInId>-<svcMajVersion>.<svcMinVersion>]\n*\n\"\nWhere:\n<svcId>\nis the Service ID derived from the Manifest, where the\nDdsServiceInter-\nfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nserviceInterfaceId\n.\n161 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

DataWriters associated with\ntrigger\ns in the\nServi-\nceInterface\ncreated in previous calls to the\nOfferService()\nmethod.\n\u000f\nIt shall remove all DDS DataWriters and DataReaders associated       "source_page": 163,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_11006] Mapping of FindService method\nd\nWhen instructed to find remote\nServices, the DDS Binding shall perform the following operations:\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11007] It shall look for an existing DDS DomainParticipant capable of\nfinding remote Services Instances. If such DomainParticipant does not exist, the\nDDS binding shall create a new one as specified in [SWS_CM_11008].\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11009] It shall iterate over the list of discovered remote DomainPar-\nticipants and look for those associated with Service Instances that: (1) match the\nfilter criteria specified in the\nFindService()\ncall, (2) have a compatible\nSer-\nviceInterface\ncontract version, and (3) have a\nServiceInterface\ncontract\nversion that is not part of a\nDdsRequiredServiceInstance\n.\nblocklisted-\nVersion\n.\n\u000f\nIt shall return a\nHandleType\nobject for every Service Instance that: (1) matches\nthe filter criteria, (2) has a compatible\nServiceInterface\ncontract version, and\n(3) has a\nServiceInterface\ncontract version that is not part of a\nDdsRe-\nquiredServiceInstance\n.\nblocklistedVersion\n. The Handle object shall\ncontain a reference to both the DomainParticipant that was used in the discovery\nphase and the DDS Publisher and Subscriber created to match the partition of\nthe remote service instance (see [SWS_CM_11009]), so that they can be used\nto create the appropriate DataWriters and DataReaders to handle remote com-\nmunication.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00005, FO_RS_Dds_00008)\n[SWS_CM_11007] Finding a DDS DomainParticipant suitable for performing\nclient-side operations\nd\nThe DDS binding shall provide client-side methods with a\nDDS DomainParticipant capable of discovering and communicating with remote DDS\nDomainParticipants assigned to the requested Service Instance(s). The configuration\nof the DomainParticipant is described in the TPS_ManifestSpecification:\n\u000f\nThe Domain ID of the DomainParticipant shall be derived from the Manifest,\nwhere the\nDdsRequiredServiceInstance\nelement defines the\ndomainId\n.\n\u000f\nThe QoS Profile of the DomainParticipant shall be derived from the Manifest,\nwhere the\nDdsRequiredServiceInstance\nelement defines the\nqosProfile\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00005, FO_RS_Dds_00008)\n[SWS_CM_11008] Creating a DDS DomainParticipant suitable for perform-\ning client-side operations\nd\nTo create a DomainParticipant capable of discovering\nand communicating with remote DDS DomainParticipants assigned to Service In-\nstances, the binding implementation shall use the configuration parameters in the\nTPS_ManifestSpecification described in [SWS_CM_11007].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_-\nCM_00200, RS_CM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00005, FO_RS_-\nDds_00008)\n163 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_11009] Discovering remote Service Instances through DDS Domain-\nParticipants\nd\nDDS DomainParticipants created or retrieved in the context of Ser-\nvice Discovery are responsible for discovering remote DomainParticipants assigned\nto ara::com Service Instances.\nTo retrieve the list of discovered Service Instances, the DDS binding shall iterate first\nthe list of remote DomainParticipants the DomainParticipant has discovered so far.\nThis shall be done by calling\nread()\non the DomainParticipant's built-in DataReader\nfor the\nDCPSParticipant\nTopic.\nDCPSParticipant\nis a standard DDS Topic de-\nfined in [20] that DomainParticipants use to inform other DomainParticipants of their\npresence in the network. Among other things,\nDCPSParticipant\nTopics propagate\nthe DomainParticipant's USER_DATA QoS Policy; therefore, these messages provide\nall the necessary information to identify remote DomainParticipants associated with\nara::com Service Instances.\nThe DDS binding shall analyze the content of the USER_DATA QoS of each remote Do-\nmainParticipant and check whether they are associated with Service Instances match-\ning the following criteria:\nIf\nrequiredServiceInstanceId\nis set to ALL, the binding shall return a new han-\ndle for each service instance found in remote DomainParticipants' USER_DATA QoS\naccording to the following pattern:\n\"ara.com://services/.\n*\n<svcId>.\n*\n\"\nElse, if\nrequiredServiceInstanceId\nis set to any value other than ALL, the bind-\ning shall return a new handle for every service instance found in remote DomainPar-\nticipants' USER_DATA QoS according to the following pattern:\n\"ara.com://services/.\n*\n<svcId>_<reqSvcInId>.\n*\n\"\nWhere:\n<svcId>\nis the corresponding\nserviceInterfaceId\n.\n<reqSvcInId>\nis the corresponding\nrequiredServiceInstanceId\n.\nIn either case, before returning new handles the binding implementation shall evaluate\nthe\nServiceInterface\ncontract version for the corresponding Service Instance in\nthe content of the USER_DATA QoS. The binding shall return a new handle only if:\n1. The\nServiceInterface\ncontract version of the discovered service instance is\ncompatible with the\nserviceInterfaceDeployment\nversion of the\nDdsRe-\nquiredServiceInstance\naccording to [RS_CM_00501].\n2. The\nServiceInterface\ncontract version is not part of any\nDdsRequiredSer-\nviceInstance\n.\nblocklistedVersion\n, according to [RS_CM_00701].\nBefore returning new handles, the binding implementation shall ensure that the Do-\nmainParticipant used in the discovery phase has one DDS Publisher and one DDS\n164 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

The Partition QoS\nof both DDS Publisher and DDS Subscriber shall contain the following partition name\nto match the partition in which the DataReaders and DataWriters associated with the\nremote service instance are operating (in consonance with [SWS_CM_11002]):\n\"ara.com://services/<svcId>_<reqSvcInId>\"\nIf the binding implementation does not find a DDS Publisher with the aforementioned\nrequirements, it shall create a new one and configure the Publisher's Partition QoS with\nthe partition name defined above. Likewise, if it does not find a DDS Subscriber with\nthose requirements, it shall create a new one and configure it accordingly.\nPublisher and Subscriber objects may be reused across proxies associated with a\nremote service instance; therefore, they shall not be removed until the enclosing Do-\nmainParticipant is destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00005, FO_RS_Dds_00008, RS_CM_00501, RS_CM_00701)\n[SWS_CM_11010] Mapping of StartFindService method\nd\nWhen instructed to start\na continuous service search, the DDS Binding shall perform the following operations:\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11007] It shall look for an existing DDS DomainParticipant capable of\nfinding remote Service Instances. If such DomainParticipant does not exist, the\nDDS binding shall create it as specified in [SWS_CM_11008].\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11011] It shall define a DDS BuiltinParticipantListener capable of call-\ning the given\nFindServiceHandler\nupon the occurrence of any of the following\nevents:\n1. A remote DomainParticipant assigned to a matching Service is discovered.\n2. A remote DomainParticipant assigned to a matching Service ceases\nto exist (i.e., the instance state is either\nNOT_ALIVE_DISPOSED\nor\nNOT_ALIVE_NO_WRITERS\n).\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11012] It shall bind the defined BuiltinParticipantListener to the Do-\nmainParticipant.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00005, FO_RS_Dds_00008)\n[SWS_CM_11011] Defining a DDS BuiltinParticipantListener\nd\nThe DDS Binding\nimplementation shall define a\nBuiltinParticipantListener\nclass to handle noti-\nfications whenever a remote DomainParticipant is discovered. This class shall derive"

If\nthe returned\nServiceHandleContainer\ncontains more than one element,\non_data_available()\nshall invoke\nFindServiceHandler\nand pass the\ncontainer as a parameter; otherwise the method shall return and perform no\nfurther action.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00005, FO_RS_Dds_00008)\n[SWS_CM_11012] Binding a BuiltinParticipantListener to a DDS DomainPartici-\npant\nd\nTo bind a\nBuiltinParticipantListener\nto a DDS DomainParticipant, the\nDDS binding implementation shall create a new\nBuiltinParticipantListener\nobject (see [SWS_CM_11011]) passing\nFindServiceHandler\nand\nrequiredSer-\nviceInstanceId\nto the listener's constructor. Then service shall then bind the newly\ncreated listener to the DomainParticipant using the\nset_listener()\nmethod with\nStatusMask = DATA_AVAILABLE_STATUS\n6\n.\nThe BuiltinParticipantListener shall be removed when the enclosing DomainParticipant\nis destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001,\nFO_RS_Dds_00005, FO_RS_Dds_00008)\n[SWS_CM_11013] Mapping of StopFindService method\nd\nWhen instructed to stop a\ncontinuous service search initiated by a previous call to\nStartFindService()\n, the\nDDS Binding shall perform the following operations:\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11007] It shall look for an existing DDS DomainParticipant capable\nof finding remote Service Instances. If such DomainParticipant does not exist,\nStopFindService()\nshall return and perform no further action.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11014] It shall unbind the\nBuiltinParticipantListener\nfrom\nthe retrieved DDS DomainParticipant\n7\n."

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00005, FO_-\nRS_Dds_00008)\n[SWS_CM_11014] Unbinding a BuiltinParticipantListener from a DDS Domain-\nParticipant\nd\nWhen instructed to unbind a\nBuiltinParticipantListener\nfrom\na DDS DomainParticipant, the DDS binding implementation service shall invoke\nthe DomainParticipant's\nset_listener()\nmethod to disable the listener. In that\ncase,\nset_listener()\nshall be called with\nStatusMask = STATUS_MASK_NONE\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00005, FO_-\nRS_Dds_00008)\n7.4.3.2 Service Discovery via Topic\n[SWS_CM_90502]\n{DRAFT}\nMapping of OfferService method\nd\nWhen instructed to\noffer a Service, the DDS Binding shall perform the following operations:\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_90503] It shall assign a DDS DomainParticipant to the Service In-\nstance.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_90504] It shall assign a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to ev-\nery\nVariableDataPrototype\ndefined in the\nServiceInterface\nin the role\nevent\n.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_90505] It shall assign a DDS Request Topic and a DDS Reply Topic,\nand create their corresponding DDS DataWriter and DataReader, to provide ac-\ncess to all\nClientServerOperation\ns defined in the\nServiceInterface\nthe\nrole\nmethod\n.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_90506] It shall assign a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to every\nField\ndefined in the\nServiceInterface\nin the role\nfield\nwith its\nhasNoti-\nfier\nattribute set to\ntrue\n.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_90507] It shall assign a DDS Request Topic and a DDS Reply Topic,\nand create their corresponding DDS DataWriter and DDS DataReader, to provide\naccess to all the\nField\ns defined in the\nServiceInterface\nin the role\nfield\nwith\nhasGetter\nand/or\nhasSetter\nattributes set to\ntrue\nvia getter/setter invo-\ncation.\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_90508] It shall advertise the Service Interface ID, Service Instance\nID, and\nServiceInterface\ncontract version via the\nara.com://services/-\ndiscovery\nDDS topic\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00008)\n[SWS_CM_90503]\n{DRAFT}\nAssigning a DDS DomainParticipant to a Service\nInstance\nd\nThe DDS Binding shall assign a DDS DomainParticipant to every Ser-\nvice Instance.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nThe Domain ID of the DomainParticipant shall be derived from the Manifest,\nwhere the\nDdsProvidedServiceInstance\nelement defines the\ndomainId\n.\n\u000f\nThe QoS Profile of the DomainParticipant shall be derived from the Manifest,\nwhere the\nDdsProvidedServiceInstance\nelement defines the\nqosProfile\n.\nBefore creating a new DomainParticipant, the DDS binding shall first look for existing\nDomainParticipants in the current process that match the configuration criteria speci-\nfied above\n8\n. If the search is successful, the binding shall assign the DomainParticipant\nfound to the Service\n9\n; otherwise, the binding shall create a new DomainParticipant\naccording to the desired configuration and assign it to the Service.\nOnce the DomainParticipant is available to the Service Instance, the binding implemen-\ntation shall create a DDS Publisher and a DDS Subscriber to enclose all DataWriters\nand DataReaders associated with the Service Instance.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00015, FO_RS_Dds_00016)\n[SWS_CM_90504]\n{DRAFT}\nAssigning a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to ev-\nery Event in the ServiceInterface\nd\nThe DDS binding shall assign a DDS Topic to\nevery\nevent\nin the\nServiceInterface\naccording to the mapping rules specified\nin [SWS_CM_11015]. Since these DDS Topics may already be available in the Do-\nmainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance (e.g., because a different Service\nInstance assigned to the same DomainParticipant may have created them), the ser-\nvice shall first look for existing Topics in the DomainParticipant matching the required\ncriteria. If the search is unsuccessful, the DomainParticipant shall create a new DDS\nTopic to represent the\nevent\nas defined in [SWS_CM_11015].\nOnce all DDS Topics representing the\nevent\ns in the\nServiceInterface\nare ready\nfor use, the DomainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance shall create one DDS\nDataWriter of the equivalent Topic per\nevent\nusing the DDS Publisher created in\n[SWS_CM_90503]. The DataWriter shall be configured according to the\nqosProfile\nspecified in the associated\nDdsEventQosProps\n.\nTopic objects may be reused across service instances; therefore, they shall not be re-\nmoved until the enclosing DomainParticipant is destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_-\n00015)\n[SWS_CM_90505]\n{DRAFT}\nAssigning a DDS Request and Reply Topic, and\nDataWriters and DataReaders, to the Methods in the ServiceInterface\nd\nThe DDS\nbinding shall instantiate a DDS Service [22] to handle requests to all the\nmethod\ns in\nthe\nServiceInterface\n."

      "source_page": 169,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nIn practice, this implies assigning a DDS Request Topic and a DDS Reply Topic to the\nDDS Service that handles those method calls according to the mapping rules spec-\nified in [SWS_CM_11100]. Since these DDS Topics may already be available in the\nDomainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance (e.g., because a different Service\nInstance assigned to the same DomainParticipant may have created them), the service\nshall first look for existing Topics in the DomainParticipant matching the required crite-\nria. If the search is unsuccessful, the DomainParticipant shall create new DDS Request\nand Reply Topics to represent the DDS Service as specified in [SWS_CM_11100].\nOnce the corresponding DDS Request and Reply Topics are ready for use, the Do-\nmainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance shall create:\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11106] A DDS DataReader of the DDS Request Topic to handle re-\nquests using the DDS Subscriber created in [SWS_CM_90503].\n\u000f\n[SWS_CM_11107] A DDS DataWriter of the DDS Reply Topic to handle replies\nusing the DDS Publisher created in [SWS_CM_90503].\nTopic objects may be reused across service instances; therefore, they shall not be re-\nmoved until the enclosing DomainParticipant is destroyed.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00200, RS_CM_00101, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_-\n00015, FO_RS_Dds_00016)\nThe handling of method calls with DDS is specified in 7.4.3.5.\n[SWS_CM_90506]\n{DRAFT}\nAssigning a DDS Topic and a DDS DataWriter to ev-\nery Field in the ServiceInterface with its hasNotifier attribute equal to true\nd\nThe\nDDS binding shall assign a DDS Topic to every\nfield\nin the\nServiceInterface\nwith its\nhasNotifier\nattribute set to\ntrue\naccording to the mapping rules specified\nin [SWS_CM_11130]. If the search is unsuccessful, the DomainParticipant shall create a new DDS\nTopic to represent the\nfield\nas defined in [SWS_CM_11130].\nOnce all DDS Topics representing the\nfield\ns in the\nServiceInterface\nare ready\nfor use, the DomainParticipant assigned to the Service Instance shall create one DDS\nDataWriter of the equivalent Topic per\nfield\nwith the\nhasNotifier\nattribute set to\ntrue\nusing the DDS Publisher created in [SWS_CM_90503]. The\n@external\nannotation is optionally\nallowed, for cases where references yield implementation benefits over values.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\nThe DDS serialization rules are defined in section 7.4.3.7.\n[SWS_CM_11017] Mapping of Send method\nd\nWhen instructed to send an event\nmessage, the DDS Binding shall construct a new sample of the equivalent DDS Topic\ndata type (see [SWS_CM_11016]) as follows:\n\u000f\nThe Instance Id field (\ninstance_id\n) shall be derived from the Manifest, where\nthe\nDdsProvidedServiceInstance\nelement defines the\nserviceInstan-\nceId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Data field (\ndata\n) shall point to the\ndata\ninput parameter of the\nSend()\nmethod.\nThat sample shall be then passed as a parameter to the\nwrite()\nmethod of the DDS\nDataWriter associated with the\nevent\n, which shall serialize the sample according\nto the serialization rules, and publish it over DDS.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201,\nFO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00015)\nThe DDS serialization rules are defined in section 7.4.3.7.\n[SWS_CM_11018] Mapping of Subscribe method\nd\nWhen instructed to subscribe to\nan event, the DDS binding shall create a DDS DataReader using the DDS Subscriber\ncreated for the proxy in [SWS_CM_11009]. To configure\nthe DataReader's cache size according to the\nmaxSampleCount\nspecified in the\nSubscribe()\nmethod call, the value of the DataReader's HISTORY QoS speci-\nfied in\nqosProfile\nshall be overridden as follows:\n176 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

This class shall derive from the standard\nDataReaderListener\nclass\n[19], specifying that the samples to be handled are of the Topic data type specified in\n[SWS_CM_11016].\nThe\nDataReaderListener\nshall implement the following methods according to the\nspecified instructions:\n\u000f\nA Constructor that initializes two member variables that hold references to an\nEventReceiveHandler\nand a\nSubscriptionStateChangeHandler\n.\n\u000f\nAn\non_data_available()\nmethod that calls the\nEventReceiveHandler\nif it\nhas been set and there are valid samples in the DataReader's cache.\n\u000f\nAn\non_subscription_matched()\nmethod that calls\nGetSubscription-\nState()\nand passes the resulting\nSubscriptionState\nto\nSubscription-\nStateChangeHandler\nif it has been set.\n\u000f\nA\nset_event_receive_handler()\nmethod that takes as an input parameter\na reference to an\nEventReceiveHandler\nand updates the member variable\nholding a reference to an\nEventReceiveHandler\nto point to the input parame-\nter.\n\u000f\nA\nset_subscription_state_change_handler()\nmethod that takes as an\ninput parameter a reference to a\nSubscriptionStateChangeHandler\nand\nupdates the member variable holding a reference to a\nSubscriptionState-\nChangeHandler\nto point to the input parameter.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00103, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_-\nRS_Dds_00016)\n[SWS_CM_11021] Mapping of Unsubscribe method\nd\nWhen instructed to unsub-\nscribe from a service event, the DDS binding shall delete the DataReader associ-\nated with the\nevent\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00104, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_-\nRS_Dds_00008)\n177 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.3.4 Handling Triggers\n[SWS_CM_10524]\n{DRAFT}\nMapping Triggers to DDS Topics\nd\nThe DDS binding\nshall map every\nTrigger\ndefined in the\nServiceInterface\nin the role\ntrigger\nto a DDS Topic. The equivalent DDS Topic shall be configured as follows:\n\u000f\nThe Topic Name shall be derived from the Manifest according to the following\nrules:\n\nIf the provided or consumed Service Instance has been\nadvertised with the\nidentifier_type\nattribute set to\nSERVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_PARTITION\nor\nSER-\nVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_INSTANCE_ID\n, then the topic name shall\nbe set to\nara.com://services/<InterfaceID>/<Major>.<Minor>\n/<TopicName>\n\nAdditionally, if the provided or consumed Service Instance has\nbeen advertised with the\nidentifier_type\nattribute set to\nSER-\nVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_PARTITION\n, then samples of this topic shall\nbe sent and received via DataWriters and DataReaders whose respective\nparent Publisher and Subscriber objects include the following partition in the\nPARTITION QoS policy:\nara.com://services/<InterfaceID>/<In-\nstanceId>\n\nFinally, if the provided or consumed Service Instance has been\nadvertised with the\nidentifier_type\nattribute set to\nSER-\nVICE_INSTANCE_TOPIC_PREFIX\n, then the topic name shall be set\nto\nara.com://services/<InterfaceID>/<InstanceID>/<Topic-\nName>\n\nWhere:\n<InterfaceID>\nis the value of\nDdsServiceInterfaceDeployment\n.\nserviceInterfaceId\n<InstanceID>\nis the value of either\nDdsProvidedServiceInstance\n.\nserviceInstanceId\nor\nDdsRequiredServiceInstance\n.\nre-\nquiredServiceInstanceId\n<Major>\nand\n<Minor>\nare the values of\nServiceInterface\n.\nma-\njorVersion\nand\nServiceInterface\n.\nminorVersion\n, respectively\n<TopicName>\nis the value of\nDdsEventDeployment\n.\ntopicName\nassoci-\nated with the\ntrigger\n\u000f\nThe Topic Data Type shall be defined as specified in [SWS_CM_10525], and shall\nbe registered under the equivalent data type name.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00005, FO_-\nRS_Dds_00007, FO_RS_Dds_00008)\n181 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10525]\n{DRAFT}\nDDS Topic data type definition\nd\nThe data type of a DDS\nTopic representing a trigger shall be constructed according to the following IDL defini-\ntion:\n1\nstruct TriggerType {\n2\n@key uint16 instanceIdentifier;\n3\n};\nWhere:\ninstance_id\nis a\n@key\nmember of the type, which identifies all samples with the\nsame\ninstance_id\nas samples of the same Topic Instance.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n[SWS_CM_10526]\n{DRAFT}\nMapping of Send method\nd\nWhen instructed to send a\ntrigger message, the DDS Binding shall construct a new sample of the equivalent DDS\nTopic data type (see [SWS_CM_10525]) as follows:\n\u000f\nThe Instance Id field (\ninstance_id\n) shall be derived from the Manifest, where\nthe\nDdsProvidedServiceInstance\nelement defines the\nserviceInstan-\nceId\n.\nThat sample shall be then passed as a parameter to the\nwrite()\nmethod of the DDS\nDataWriter associated with the\ntrigger\n, which shall serialize the sample according\nto the serialization rules, and publish it over DDS.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201,\nFO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00015)\nThe DDS serialization rules are defined in section 7.4.3.7.\n[SWS_CM_10527]\n{DRAFT}\nMapping of Subscribe method\nd\nWhen instructed to sub-\nscribe to a trigger, the DDS binding shall create a DDS DataReader using the DDS\nSubscriber created for the proxy in [SWS_CM_11009] or [SWS_CM_90513]. The rules\nto create the DataReader are specified in [SWS_CM_10528].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_-\nCM_00103, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00016)\n[SWS_CM_10528]\n{DRAFT}\nCreating a DDS DataReader for trigger subscrip-\ntion\nd\nThe DDS binding shall create a DDS DataReader for the Topic associated\nwith the\ntrigger\n(see [SWS_CM_10524]). If the provided or consumed Service\nInstance has been advertised with the\nidentifier_type\nattribute set to\nSER-\nVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_PARTITION\n, to ensure the proxy communicates only\nwith the service instance it is bound to, the binding implementation shall use the DDS\nSubscriber created in [SWS_CM_11009] (whose partition name is\n\"ara.com://-\nservices/<svcId>_<reqSvcInId>\"\n) to create the DataReader.\nThe DataReader shall be configured as follows:\n\u000f\nDataReaderQos\nshall be set as specified in the Manifest, where the\nDdsEven-\ntQosProps\nelement defines the\nqosProfile\nthat shall be used.\n\u000f\nListener\nshall be an instance of the\nDataReaderListener\nclass specified in\n[SWS_CM_11020].\n182 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_11150] Creating a DataWriter to handle get/set responses on the\nserver side\nd\nThe DDS binding shall create a DDS DataWriter for the Reply Topic as-\nsociated with the getters and setters of the\nfield\ns of the\nServiceInterface\n(see\n[SWS_CM_11146]).\nIf the provided or consumed Service Instance has been advertised with the\nidenti-\nfier_type\nattribute set to\nSERVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_PARTITION\n, the bind-\ning implementation shall use the DDS Publisher created in [SWS_CM_11002] (whose\npartition name is\n\"ara.com://services/<svcId>_<svcInId>\"\n) to create the\nDataWriter.\nThe DataWriter shall be configured as follows:\n\u000f\nDataWriterQos\nshall be set as specified in the Manifest, where the\nDdsField-\nQosProps\nelement defines the\nqosProfile\nthat shall be used.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00005)\n[SWS_CM_11151] Calling get/set method associated with a field from the client\nside\nd\nWhen instructed to call the\nGet()\nor\nSet()\nmethod associated with a\nField\nfrom the client side, the DDS binding shall construct a new sample of the corre-\nsponding Request Topican instance of the Request Topic data type defined in\n[SWS_CM_11145]as follows:\n\u000f\nTo initialize the\nRequestHeader\nobject,\n\nrequestId\nshall be set by the underlying DDS implementation according\nto the rules specified in [22].\n\ninstanceName\nshall be set by the binding implementation to the\nservi-\nceInstanceId\nof the remote service instance.\n\u000f\nTo initialize the\n<svcId>Field_Call\nobject, the binding implementation shall\nfirst select the appropriate union case (as specified in [SWS_CM_11145], the\nhash of the field getter/setter's name is the union discriminator that selects the\nunion case). Then,\n\nIf the call corresponds to a getter, the binding shall leave the\ndummy\nmember\nof the\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>_In\nstructure unset.\n\nElse, if the call corresponds to a setter, the binding shall set accordingly the\nonly member of the\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldName>_In\nstructure with\nthe new value for the field.\nThat sample shall then be passed as a parameter to the\nwrite()\nmethod of the DDS\nDataWriter created in [SWS_CM_11147] to handle get/set requests on the client side,\nwhich shall serialize the sample according to the DDS serialization rules, and pub-\nlish it over DDS.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213,\nRS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_-\nDds_00015)\n209 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe DDS serialization rules are defined in section 7.4.3.7.\n[SWS_CM_11152] Notifying the client of the response to the get/set method\ncall\nd\nTo notify the client application of a response as a result of call to a\nGet()\nor\nSet()\nmethod associated with a\nField\n, the DDS binding implementation shall\ninvoke the\nset_value()\noperation (see [SWS_CORE_00345] and [SWS_CORE_-\n00346]) with the value of the corresponding\nresult_\nmember of either the\n<sv-\ncId>Field_Get<FieldName>_Result\nstructure, for get operations; or\n<svcId>\nField_Set<FieldName>_Out\n, for set operations.\nThe associated set operation shall be performed upon the reception of a new Reply\nTopic sample by the corresponding DDS DataReader (see [SWS_CM_11148]). The\nDDS binding shall use the DataReader's\ntake()\nmethod to process the sample. More-\nover, to correlate a request with a response, the binding shall compare the\nheader.-\nrelatedRequestsId\nof the received sample with the original\nrequestId\nthat was\nsent in [SWS_CM_11151]\n13\n.       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.3.8 End-to-end communication protection\nThe present DDS network binding is defined in terms of interactions between\nara::\ncom\nAPIs and standard DDS APIs. Hence, End-to-end communication protection as\ndescribed in sections 7.6.1 and 7.6.2 doesn't apply, because API calls can't be check-\nsummed or payloaded the same way serialized messages are.\nBy no means does this imply that DDS is exempt from E2E protection assurances,\nthey are simply provided by the DDS middleware. Please find below the different kinds\nof faults defined in [7] (derived from ISO-26262-6:2011, annex D.2.4) and their corre-\nsponding DDS/RTPS protection mechanism:\n\u000f\nRepetition, loss, insertion, incorrect sequence, information from a sender re-\nceived by only a subset of receivers, and blocking access to a communica-\ntion channel: submessage 64-bit sequence number, as defined in [20] section\n8.3.5.4 \"SequenceNumber\", and additional SequenceNumber-typed fields in sec-\ntion 8.3.7 \"RTPS Submessages\"\n\u000f\nDelay of information and blocking access to a communication channel:\nLA-\nTENCY_BUDGET\nQuality of Service policy, as defined in [19] section 2.2.3.8 \"LA-\nTENCY_BUDGET\"\n\u000f\nMasquerade or incorrect addressing of information: DDS Security authentication\nplugin, as defined in [26] section 8.3 \"Authentication Plugin\"\n\u000f\nCorruption of information, asymmetric information sent from a sender to mul-\ntiple receivers:\nrtpsMessageChecksum\nunder HeaderExtension submessage\n([RTPS 2.5 or higher]). In absence of this feature, [26] also provides message\nintegrity verification built into its message authentication protocol\n\u000f\nTranslation of these fault conditions into\nara::com::e2e::ProfileCheck-\nStatus\nvalues depends on the specific capacities of the DDS implementation\nto report per-sample the status of the aforementioned protection measures (se-\nquence numbers, latency budget, message authentications, checksums)\n7.5 Security\nIn the following chapter the behavior according to the meta-model of access control\nand secure communication shall be described.\n7.5.1 IAM\nAccess control for Communication Management allows to restrict the instances and\nelements of services that a local application or a\nremote subject\n(e.g., a remote ECU)\nmay request to access. Having access control in place reduces the potential damage\n215 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P216_382",

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthat a compromised application (in case of local IAM) or a compromised ECU (in case\nof remote IAM) can cause.\nFigure 7.17 demonstrates an example scenario where local IAM and remote IAM can\ntake place. Upon a method call from a service, the client's request will be checked by\nthe local IAM to ensure that the application is issuing a legitimate request based on its\nconfigured access rights. After successful authorization, the request will be forwarded\nto the machine where the service is running. When the request arrives at the recipient\nmachine, the remote IAM takes place and a check will be performed to verify if such a\nrequest coming from the given sender ECU was envisioned."

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.17: Local and Remote Identity and Access Management\nThe following assumption has to be held true to realize access control:\n1. Communication between two applications has to be realized by using ara::com\ninterfaces Communication Management to enable access control.\nAll access permissions for Communication Management are modeled using\nComGrant\nmodel elements. A\nComGrant\ncan be used to model access permissions that either\napply to a\nMachine\n-local\nProcess\nor to a remote subject, i.e., either a local Process\nor a remote entity can be the\nsubject\nof the access control policy: If a\nComGrant\nreferences an\nAbstractIamRemoteSubject\nin the role\nremoteSubject\n, then the\nsubjects of the\nComGrant\nare all remote entities that can be identified using the in-\nformation specified in the referenced\nAbstractIamRemoteSubject\n. If a\nComGrant\ndoes not reference any\nremoteSubject\n, then the subjects of the\nComGrant\nare all\nProcess\nes referenced in the role\nprocess\nby\nServiceInstanceToPortProto-\ntypeMapping\ns which reference an\nAdaptivePlatformServiceInstance\nin the\nrole\nserviceInstance\nthat is referenced by the\nComGrant\nin the role\nserviceIn-\nstance\n.\nLocal access control and remote access control may be enforced independently from\neach other.\n216 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.5.1.1 Configuration of Access Control\nWhile Identity and Access Management (IAM) serves as an umbrella for access control\non the\nAdaptive Platform\n, the enforcement of access control is implemented in\ndifferent functional clusters such as CM. If no IAM Functional Cluster is instantiated on\na\nMachine\n, then no enforcement of access control by CM is expected.\n[SWS_CM_10492]\n{DRAFT}\nIAM Module Instantiation\nd\nIf no\nIamModuleInstanti-\nation\nis defined on the Machine, CM shall perform no access control, i.e., no access\nto any service shall be restricted because of missing\nComGrant\ns.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00002)\nDepending on the architecture and the security model, all local\nProcess\nes might be\ntrusted, thus not requiring local access control. Furthermore, it is possible that all\nremote ECUs are trusted, e.g., because access control is already performed locally.\nFor these cases, there are two configuration options to enable remote access control\nand local access control independently.\n[SWS_CM_10493]\n{DRAFT}\nLocal Access Control Activation\nd\nIf\nIamModuleIn-\nstantiation\n.\nlocalComAccessControlEnabled\nis defined and is set to false, CM\nshall perform no local access control, i.e., no access to any service from a local\nPro-\ncess\nshall be restricted because of missing\nComGrant\ns. If\nIamModuleInstanti-\nation\nis defined on the Machine and\nIamModuleInstantiation\n.\nlocalComAc-\ncessControlEnabled\nis not defined or is set to true, CM shall perform local access\ncontrol.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00002)\n[SWS_CM_10494]\n{DRAFT}\nRemote Access Control Activation\nd\nIf\nIamModuleIn-\nstantiation\n.\nremoteAccessControlEnabled\nis defined and is set to false, CM\nshall perform no remote access control, i.e., no access to any service from a remote\nsubject shall be restricted because of missing\nComGrant\ns. If\nIamModuleInstanti-\nation\nis defined on the Machine and\nIamModuleInstantiation\n.\nremoteAccess-\nControlEnabled\nis not defined or is set to true, CM shall perform remote access\ncontrol.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00002)\n[SWS_CM_10542]\n{DRAFT}\nLocal access control on providing service instances\nd\nIf a\nProcess\nrequests to provide a service instance or any element thereof, but there\nexists no\nComOfferServiceGrant\nthat\n\u000f\ndoes not reference any remote subject in the role\nremoteSubject\nand\n\u000f\nreferences the requested\nProvidedApServiceInstance\nin the role\nservi-\nceInstance\nand the\nProvidedApServiceInstance\nis referenced by a\nSer-\nviceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nin the role\nserviceInstance\nand the\nServiceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nreferences the re-\nquesting\nProcess\nin the role\nprocess\n,\nthen Communication Management shall drop the request.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00001, RS_-\nIAM_00002)\n[SWS_CM_90006]\n{DRAFT}\nLocal access control on service discovery\nd\nIf a\nPro-\ncess\nrequests to find a service, but there exists no\nComGrant\nthat\n217 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

Then, it\nhas to be decided whether the access is allowed according to the modeled grants.\nThere are currently three ways to authenticate a remote subject:\n\u000f\nTLS:\nIf the remote subject is connected via (D)TLS secure communication, prop-\nerties of this TLS connection and the used certificates can be used for authenti-\ncating the remote subject.\n\u000f\nIPsec:\nIf IPsec is used to establish secure communication, IP related informa-\ntion specified for IPsec configuration can be used for authenticating the remote\nsubject.\n219 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe configuration of SecOc and TLS security protocols has a dependency on the net-\nwork binding:\n\u000f\nFor SOME/IP network binding AUTOSAR allows the configuration of secure com-\nmunication for a ServiceInterface by configuring either\nTlsSecureComProps\nmeta-class or\nSecOcSecureComProps\nmeta-class . Both are specialization\nof\nSecureComProps\nclass that is referenced by\nServiceInstanceToMa-\nchineMapping\n. In the case of SecOc additionally\nServiceInterfaceEle-\nmentSecureComConfig\nneeds to be defined and it determines the configura-\ntion settings for the individual ServiceInterface elements. When\nTlsSecure-\nComProps\nis configured, all the service interface elements are secured and\nServiceInterfaceElementSecureComConfig\nis not used.\n\u000f\nFor Signal based network binding, only SecOc configuration is possible, and\nthe configuration is determined by\nSecureCommunicationAuthentication-\nProps\nof a SecuredIPdu referenced by the PduTriggering.\nSecureComProps\nis\nnot used in the context of signal-based network binding.\n\u000f\nFor DDS Network binding, DDS Transport Security over TCP (TLS), DDS Trans-\nport Security over UDP (DTLS) and DDS Security [26] (as transport-independent\nsecurity) are valid, independent and mutually exclusive choices for securing un-\nderlying DDS communications.\nThe configuration of Ipsec (IPSecConfig) in aggregated by a NetworkEndpoint there-\nfore it is independent of the network binding.\nSOME/IP supports one-to-many (unicast) and many-to-many (multicast) communica-\ntion paradigms. These paradigms may switch at runtime for events (see\nmulticast-\nThreshold\n).\nIt is therefore important to be aware of the limitations of the secure channel approach:\n\u000f\nConfidentiality of events\nIf events are transported using UDP and may be sent using multicast, they can-\nnot be guaranteed confidential due to the fact that only SecOC can be used to\nsecure multicast communication and SecOC does not offer confidentiality. This\nrestriction does not apply to DDS Security.\n7.5.2.1 Creation and use of secure channels\n7.5.2.1.1 SOME/IP and DDS network binding\n[SWS_CM_90101]\n{DRAFT}\nSecure UDP and TCP channel creation for TLS, DTLS\nand SecOC\nd\nThe Communication Management software shall create secure UDP\nchannels according to the input for all\nSecureComProps\nreferenced by\nService-\nInstanceToMachineMapping\nin the role\nsecureComPropsForUdp\n. The Commu-\nnication Management software shall create secure TCP channels according to the in-\nput for all\nSecureComProps\nreferenced by\nServiceInstanceToMachineMapping\n223 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

In the configuration the appropri-\nate secure channel is identified by examining the references to\nSecureComProps\nof\nServiceInstanceToMachineMapping\nfor the\nAdaptivePlatformServiceIn-\nstance\nthat is mapped to an\nEthernetCommunicationConnector\nof a\nMachine\nby this\nServiceInstanceToMachineMapping\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00801, RS_CM_00803)\nThe actual secure channel to be created is determined by the concrete sub-class of\nthe\nSecureComProps\nbase-class.\n[SWS_CM_90201]\n{DRAFT}\nSecure TLS and DTLS channel creation in the\nDDS Network Binding\nd\nSecure channels shall be created as specified in\n[SWS_CM_90101].\nc\n(RS_CM_00801)\n[SWS_CM_90202]\n{DRAFT}\nUsing TLS and DTLS secure channels in the DDS Net-\nwork Binding\nd\nSecure channels shall be used as specified in [SWS_CM_90102].\nc\n(RS_CM_00801, RS_CM_00803)\n7.5.2.2 DDS Security\nDDS Security, as defined in [26], is a complementary standard to DDS, providing\ntransport-independent security measures (authentication, secrecy, non-repudiation, in-\ntegrity, access control and logging) without requiring changes to application logic.\nMapping DDS Service Interface and Instance Deployment models, as well as IAM\nCommunications Grant models, to DDS QoS policies, and DDS Security certificate,\ngovernance and permission files is defined by [29].\n[SWS_CM_90218]\n{DRAFT}\nEnforcement of IAM grants through DDS Security\nd\nAdaptive Applications providing or requiring Service Interface Instances through the\nDDS Network Binding shall enforce, when provided, deployed DDS Security policies.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00001, RS_IAM_00002, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00009)\n7.5.2.3 SecOC\nThe Secure Onboard Communication (SecOC) feature is embedded into the Adap-\ntive Communication Management. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Kommunikationsmodell</h4>\n<p><code>ara::com</code> ist die standardisierte Anwendungsoberfläche des Communication-Management-Funktionsclusters. Der Cluster baut und überwacht Kommunikationspfade zwischen Anwendungen auf derselben oder auf verschiedenen Maschinen; die konkrete interne Middleware-Architektur bleibt hingegen Implementierungssache. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1\">SWS CM §7.1.1 „Architectural concepts“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2\">SWS CM §7.1.2 „Design decisions“</a> ordnen die API als protokollabstrahierte, serviceorientierte Schnittstelle ein.</p>\n<p>Aus einem modellierten Service Interface entstehen zwei Rollen: Der Proxy ist die lokale Repräsentation für den Consumer, der Skeleton verbindet die Provider-Implementierung mit der Transportinfrastruktur. Methoden, Events, Fields und Triggers sind die vier vorgesehenen Kommunikationsformen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.1\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.1 „Proxy/Skeleton Architecture“</a>, <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.2\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.2 „Means of Communication“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3\">SWS CM §7.1.3 „Communication paradigms and Definitions“</a> beschreiben diese Arbeitsteilung.</p>\n<h4>Vom Dienstangebot zur Nutzung</h4>\n<p>Auf Provider-Seite wird ein Skeleton erzeugt und angeboten. Auf Consumer-Seite liefert ein einmaliges <code>FindService</code> die aktuell bekannten Instanzen; <code>StartFindService</code> überwacht Verfügbarkeitsänderungen. Ein Handle identifiziert eine gefundene Instanz und wird zur Proxy-Erzeugung verwendet. Bei temporärer Nichtverfügbarkeit soll der Kommunikationspfad bei einem späteren Angebot erneut aufgebaut werden. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.1\">SWS CM §7.5.1 „Offer service“</a>, <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.10\">SWS CM §7.5.10 „Find service“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.11\">SWS CM §7.5.11 „Service proxy creation“</a> liefern die Funktionssemantik.</p>\n<h4>Daten- und Interaktionsformen</h4>\n<p>Events transportieren Daten an angemeldete Consumer; Triggers benutzen denselben Subscription-Mechanismus ohne Nutzdaten. Methoden modellieren Request/Response und können ein <code>Future</code> bereitstellen. Ein Field kombiniert lesenden und schreibenden Methodencharakter mit der Benachrichtigung über Wertänderungen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.3\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.3 „Event and Trigger based communication“</a>, <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.4\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.4 „Method based communication“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.5\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.5 „Field based communication“</a> erklären die Anwendungssicht.</p>\n<h4>Betriebsregeln und Sicherheitskontext</h4>\n<p><code>Subscribe()</code> ist asynchron: Erst <code>kSubscribed</code> im Status oder im Status-Handler belegt eine tatsächlich etablierte Subscription. Empfangene Samples haben einen kontrollierten Besitzübergang und müssen vor Abmeldung oder Proxy-Zerstörung zurückgegeben sein. <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_12006\">[SWS_CM_12006]</a> und <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00085\">[SWS_CM_00085]</a> sind dafür die maßgeblichen Regeln. E2E-Schutz ergänzt die Datenübertragung um pro Sample auswertbare Statusinformationen; SecOC kann Freshness-Value-Management über die Plattform-Erweiterung einsetzen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4\">SWS CM §7.4 „Safety“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.3.2\">SWS CM §7.3.2 „Secure Communication“</a> geben den übergreifenden Rahmen vor.</p>\n<h4>Instanzbezug und Bindungsabstraktion</h4>\n<p>Anwendungscode verwendet typischerweise einen logischen <code>InstanceSpecifier</code>; das Manifest löst ihn auf einen oder mehrere bindungsspezifische <code>InstanceIdentifier</code> auf. Damit kann derselbe Anwendungscode mit einer deploymentseitig anderen Bindung arbeiten, ohne deren Repräsentation zu interpretieren. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.8.1\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 „Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers“</a> und <a Quelle: <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.8.1\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 „Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers“</a>.</p><h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>\n<p>Die einmalige Dienstsuche <code>FindService()</code> liefert die zu diesem Zeitpunkt passenden Service-Handles; die Ergebnisliste kann leer sein, wenn aktuell keine passende Service-Instanz existiert. Ein technischer Suchfehler wird dagegen als <code>ara::core::Result</code>-Fehler gemeldet, für den die API unter anderem <code>ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure</code> festlegt. Die kontinuierliche Suche mit <code>StartFindService()</code> meldet Verfügbarkeitsänderungen über ihren Handler, der den Container aller passenden Instanzen erhält. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.5.3.2\">EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.2 „RadarService Proxy Class Example“</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00122\">[SWS_CM_00122]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00383\">[SWS_CM_00383]</a></p>\n<p>Ein Event-Abonnement hat die Zustände <code>kNotSubscribed</code>, <code>kSubscriptionPending</code> und <code>kSubscribed</code>. Da <code>Subscribe()</code> den Abonnementauftrag zunächst nur entgegennimmt, kann der Status bei der Abfrage noch <code>kSubscriptionPending</code> sein; <code>GetSubscriptionState()</code> und <code>SetSubscriptionStateChangeHandler()</code> machen den wirksamen Zustand zugänglich. Wird der Dienst vorübergehend nicht verfügbar, meldet der Handler <code>kSubscriptionPending</code>; nach erfolgreichem Wiederabonnement meldet er <code>kSubscribed</code>. Die Communication-Management-Implementierung muss ein aktives Abonnement nach zeitweiliger Nichtverfügbarkeit wiederherstellen. Hält die Anwendung mehr <code>SamplePtr</code>-Objekte als bei <code>Subscribe()</code> zugesagt, liefert <code>GetNewSamples()</code> den Fehler <code>ComErrc::kMaxSamplesExceeded</code>; dabei können Samples übersprungen worden sein. <a class=\"swsref\" Die verlinkten Teilnehmer sind APPLICATION INTERFACE. Quellen: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00196\">[SWS_CM_00196]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_10440\">[SWS_CM_10440]</a> <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.7.4.1.2.5.3\">SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.5.3 „E2E error notification“</a>.</p>\n<p>Bei E2E-geschützten Events kann die Anwendung pro <code>SamplePtr</code> mit <code>GetProfileCheckStatus()</code> das Ergebnis der E2E-Prüfung einsehen, beispielsweise <code>kOk</code>, <code>kRepeated</code>, <code>kWrongSequence</code> oder <code>kError</code>. Der <code>SMState</code> verdichtet die Prüfhistorie zur aktuellen E2E-Überwachung; nur bei <code>kValid</code> und einem nicht fehlerhaften Profilstatus darf das zuletzt geprüfte Sample verwendet werden. Schlägt die E2E-Prüfung einer Methodenantwort fehl, setzt die Implementierung einen Fehler aus <code>ara::com::e2e::ComE2EErrorDomain</code> in das zugehörige Promise und damit in das Future-Ergebnis. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Kommunikationsmodell</h4>
<p><code>ara::com</code> ist die standardisierte Anwendungsoberfläche des Communication-Management-Funktionsclusters. Der Cluster baut und überwacht Kommunikationspfade zwischen Anwendungen auf derselben oder auf verschiedenen Maschinen; die konkrete interne Middleware-Architektur bleibt hingegen Implementierungssache. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1">SWS CM §7.1.1 „Architectural concepts“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS CM §7.1.2 „Design decisions“</a> ordnen die API als protokollabstrahierte, serviceorientierte Schnittstelle ein.</p>
<p>Aus einem modellierten Service Interface entstehen zwei Rollen: Der Proxy ist die lokale Repräsentation für den Consumer, der Skeleton verbindet die Provider-Implementierung mit der Transportinfrastruktur. Methoden, Events, Fields und Triggers sind die vier vorgesehenen Kommunikationsformen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.1">EXP ARAComAPI §4.1 „Proxy/Skeleton Architecture“</a>, <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.2">EXP ARAComAPI §4.2 „Means of Communication“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3">SWS CM §7.1.3 „Communication paradigms and Definitions“</a> beschreiben diese Arbeitsteilung.</p>
<h4>Vom Dienstangebot zur Nutzung</h4>
<p>Auf Provider-Seite wird ein Skeleton erzeugt und angeboten. Auf Consumer-Seite liefert ein einmaliges <code>FindService</code> die aktuell bekannten Instanzen; <code>StartFindService</code> überwacht Verfügbarkeitsänderungen. Ein Handle identifiziert eine gefundene Instanz und wird zur Proxy-Erzeugung verwendet. Bei temporärer Nichtverfügbarkeit soll der Kommunikationspfad bei einem späteren Angebot erneut aufgebaut werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.1">SWS CM §7.5.1 „Offer service“</a>, <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.10">SWS CM §7.5.10 „Find service“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.11">SWS CM §7.5.11 „Service proxy creation“</a> liefern die Funktionssemantik.</p>
<h4>Daten- und Interaktionsformen</h4>
<p>Events transportieren Daten an angemeldete Consumer; Triggers benutzen denselben Subscription-Mechanismus ohne Nutzdaten. Methoden modellieren Request/Response und können ein <code>Future</code> bereitstellen. Ein Field kombiniert lesenden und schreibenden Methodencharakter mit der Benachrichtigung über Wertänderungen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.3">EXP ARAComAPI §4.3 „Event and Trigger based communication“</a>, <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.4">EXP ARAComAPI §4.4 „Method based communication“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.5">EXP ARAComAPI §4.5 „Field based communication“</a> erklären die Anwendungssicht.</p>
<h4>Betriebsregeln und Sicherheitskontext</h4>
<p><code>Subscribe()</code> ist asynchron: Erst <code>kSubscribed</code> im Status oder im Status-Handler belegt eine tatsächlich etablierte Subscription. Empfangene Samples haben einen kontrollierten Besitzübergang und müssen vor Abmeldung oder Proxy-Zerstörung zurückgegeben sein. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_12006">[SWS_CM_12006]</a> und <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00085">[SWS_CM_00085]</a> sind dafür die maßgeblichen Regeln. E2E-Schutz ergänzt die Datenübertragung um pro Sample auswertbare Statusinformationen; SecOC kann Freshness-Value-Management über die Plattform-Erweiterung einsetzen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4">SWS CM §7.4 „Safety“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.3.2">SWS CM §7.3.2 „Secure Communication“</a> geben den übergreifenden Rahmen vor.</p>
<h4>Instanzbezug und Bindungsabstraktion</h4>
<p>Anwendungscode verwendet typischerweise einen logischen <code>InstanceSpecifier</code>; das Manifest löst ihn auf einen oder mehrere bindungsspezifische <code>InstanceIdentifier</code> auf. Damit kann derselbe Anwendungscode mit einer deploymentseitig anderen Bindung arbeiten, ohne deren Repräsentation zu interpretieren. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.8.1">EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 „Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.21">SWS CM §7.5.21 „Instance Specifier Translation“</a> beschreiben die Übersetzung.</p><div class="diagram" id="diag-service-rollen"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewbox="0.00 0.00 585.00 96.00" style="max-width:780px">

</div><p class="diagram-note">Aktivitätsdiagramm: Der logische <code>InstanceSpecifier</code> wird gegen das Manifest auf eine oder mehrere bindungsspezifische IDs abgebildet. Quelle: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.8.1">EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 „Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers“</a>.</p><h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>
<p>Die einmalige Dienstsuche <code>FindService()</code> liefert die zu diesem Zeitpunkt passenden Service-Handles; die Ergebnisliste kann leer sein, wenn aktuell keine passende Service-Instanz existiert. Ein technischer Suchfehler wird dagegen als <code>ara::core::Result</code>-Fehler gemeldet, für den die API unter anderem <code>ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure</code> festlegt. Die kontinuierliche Suche mit <code>StartFindService()</code> meldet Verfügbarkeitsänderungen über ihren Handler, der den Container aller passenden Instanzen erhält. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.5.3.2">EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.2 „RadarService Proxy Class Example“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00122">[SWS_CM_00122]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00383">[SWS_CM_00383]</a></p>
<p>Ein Event-Abonnement hat die Zustände <code>kNotSubscribed</code>, <code>kSubscriptionPending</code> und <code>kSubscribed</code>. Da <code>Subscribe()</code> den Abonnementauftrag zunächst nur entgegennimmt, kann der Status bei der Abfrage noch <code>kSubscriptionPending</code> sein; <code>GetSubscriptionState()</code> und <code>SetSubscriptionStateChangeHandler()</code> machen den wirksamen Zustand zugänglich. Wird der Dienst vorübergehend nicht verfügbar, meldet der Handler <code>kSubscriptionPending</code>; nach erfolgreichem Wiederabonnement meldet er <code>kSubscribed</code>. Die Communication-Management-Implementierung muss ein aktives Abonnement nach zeitweiliger Nichtverfügbarkeit wiederherstellen. Hält die Anwendung mehr <code>SamplePtr</code>-Objekte als bei <code>Subscribe()</code> zugesagt, liefert <code>GetNewSamples()</code> den Fehler <code>ComErrc::kMaxSamplesExceeded</code>; dabei können Samples übersprungen worden sein. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00310">[SWS_CM_00310]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00333">[SWS_CM_00333]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00315">[SWS_CM_00315]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00701">[SWS_CM_00701]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.5.3.5.2">EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.5.2 „Monitoring Event Subscription“</a></p>

<p class="diagram-note">Zustandsdiagramm: Übergänge des Event-Abonnements bei Dienstverlust und automatischer Wiederherstellung. Quellen: <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00310">[SWS_CM_00310]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00315">[SWS_CM_00315]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.5.3.5.2">EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.5.2 „Monitoring Event Subscription“</a>.</p>
<p>Ein Request/Response-Methodenaufruf gibt sofort ein <code>ara::core::Future<Output></code> zurück. Darüber werden Ergebnis und mögliche Fehler abgefragt: Bei einer konfigurierten Anwendungsfehlerantwort enthält das Ergebnis einen <code>ara::core::ErrorCode</code> aus der Domäne des <code>ApApplicationError</code>; für einen nicht mehr verfügbaren Dienst ist <code>ComErrc::kServiceNotAvailable</code> festgelegt. Erkennt die Plattform lokal einen Fehler, der den bereits ausgelösten Remote-Aufruf scheitern lässt, muss sie das zugehörige Future mit <code>ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure</code> bereitstellen. Eine eigene Timeout-Überwachung für Methodenaufrufe bietet <code>ara::com</code> nicht; bei verlorener Antwort können blockierende Future-Operationen daher unbegrenzt warten. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00196">[SWS_CM_00196]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_10440">[SWS_CM_10440]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.7.4.1.2.5.3">SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.5.3 „E2E error notification“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=paragraph.7.4.1.2.6">SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.6 „Timeout supervision“</a></p>

<p class="diagram-note">Sequenzdiagramm: Ein Request/Response-Methodenaufruf stellt Anwendungs- und Verfügbarkeitsfehler über das zurückgegebene Future bereit. Die verlinkten Teilnehmer sind APPLICATION INTERFACE. Quellen: <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00196">[SWS_CM_00196]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_10440">[SWS_CM_10440]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.7.4.1.2.5.3">SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.5.3 „E2E error notification“</a>.</p>
<p>Bei E2E-geschützten Events kann die Anwendung pro <code>SamplePtr</code> mit <code>GetProfileCheckStatus()</code> das Ergebnis der E2E-Prüfung einsehen, beispielsweise <code>kOk</code>, <code>kRepeated</code>, <code>kWrongSequence</code> oder <code>kError</code>. Der <code>SMState</code> verdichtet die Prüfhistorie zur aktuellen E2E-Überwachung; nur bei <code>kValid</code> und einem nicht fehlerhaften Profilstatus darf das zuletzt geprüfte Sample verwendet werden. Schlägt die E2E-Prüfung einer Methodenantwort fehl, setzt die Implementierung einen Fehler aus <code>ara::com::e2e::ComE2EErrorDomain</code> in das zugehörige Promise und damit in das Future-Ergebnis. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_90420">[SWS_CM_90420]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_90421">[SWS_CM_90421]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_12021">[SWS_CM_12021]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_90422">[SWS_CM_90422]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_90477">[SWS_CM_90477]</a></p>
